articles.title: Spectacular Action Man images by released by widow from Norwich
articles.summary: Celebrations for 60 years of Action Man include a book of a late photographer's dramatic images.
articles.body:
A widow has marked what would have been her late husband's 50th birthday by publishing a book of his imaginative Action Man photos.

Steve Gilmour, from Norwich, was a graphic designer and had taken over 100 photos of the classic plastic toy figures over two years in various imaginative poses.

He died aged 45 in May 2022, less than a year since being diagnosed with a rare brain tumour, a grade four gliosarcoma.

His wife, Hannah Colby, said: "Steve was the most creative and imaginative person that I've ever met. He had a fantastic brain, wonderful mind."

Action Man was first produced by Leicestershire-based Palitoy in 1966 and was based on the US toy doll GI Joe. It has had a range of clothes - mostly military, but also costumes including astronaut, deep sea diver and cricketer.

Gilmour was diagnosed in August 2021 and went through radiotherapy, chemotherapy and an operation.

In January 2022, he was told that he had been given the all-clear and that his cancer was in retreat - but it returned two months later and he died that May.

The book in his memory, titled Lights, Camera, Action Man, was launched on Sunday at an official Action Man convention in North Weald Village Hall in Essex, to celebrate 60 years of the toy - which has undergone a range of physical changes over the years, as well as an ever-expanding range of dolls' costumes.

The couple met in 2020 when Colby booked a band which Gilmour was the drummer in. She recalled there being "an instant attraction".

She said that it was a mixture of the pandemic and Steve being made redundant that gave him the time to develop his creative skills and take the photographs - which he shared on social media under the name @toywithit.

According to Cancer Research UK, a glioblastoma (which a grade four gliosarcoma is a variant of) is a fast-growing type of brain tumour and is the most common type of cancerous primary brain tumour in adults.

Following Steve's death, his wife established a fundraising group in his memory to support Brain Tumour Research. The group is named Band Together, with links to the bands he was a face of in Norfolk's music scene.

Rob Wisdom, an Action Man collector and enthusiast, worked with Hannah to preserve Gilmour's work in the book and said: "Steve was a one-off, he really was.

"I think there's a child in all of us and Steve embodied that."

Gilmour's friend Adam Jarrett was also at the convention to celebrate the book launch.

He added: "That particular disease [brain tumours] does take a lot of people who are very much young and there is no fairness to it, but it's nice to know that in his memory we're able to keep his work alive, his hobbies alive."

According to the Brain Tumour Research charity, brain tumours kill more children and adults under the age of 40 than any other cancer.

Money raised from the book will go to that charity.

Colby said: "Anything I can do to further research [to give] other people a chance of life, I will do it without question."

The book features 130 images of Action Man figures in dramatic and imaginative scenarios.

Colby added: "Losing Steve felt like the tragic end to a chapter, but through Lights, Camera, Action Man, his story continues."

A Brain Tumour Research spokesperson said: "We are incredibly grateful to Hannah for turning Steve's passion into something that will help drive change for future patients.

"Through this beautiful collection of photographs, Steve's creativity and spirit will continue to inspire others while raising vital funds for research."

articles.title: Menino ganha surpresa de bombeiros no aniversário de 3 anos no Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: José Ravi, de 3 anos, fez aniversário na última sexta-feira (30) e pediu para a mãe convidar os bombeiros para a festinha de aniversário dele em Xapuri. Sem saber que o convite tinha sido aceito, criança foi surpreendida pela presença dos militares.
articles.summary: José Ravi, de 3 anos, fez aniversário na última sexta-feira (30) e pediu para a mãe convidar os bombeiros para a festinha de aniversário dele em Xapuri.
articles.body:
👨🏼‍🚒🚒 Fã do Corpo de Bombeiros, o pequeno José Ravi ganhou uma surpresa dos bombeiros de Xapuri, interior do Acre, no aniversário de 3 anos, na última sexta-feira (30). Os militares participaram da festinha da criança, mostraram uma das viaturas da equipe, ligaram a sirene e fizeram a alegria da criançada.

Um vídeo gravado pelos familiares mostra a equipe de militares chegando à residência da família de José. A criançada fica animada com a presença dos bombeiros e José Ravi fica surpreso. (Veja vídeo acima).

As imagens da festinha foram postadas em uma rede social do Corpo de Bombeiros de Xapuri.

"O Corpo de Bombeiros Militar teve a alegria de participar de um momento muito especial: o aniversário de um pequeno admirador da nossa corporação. Foi uma oportunidade de compartilhar carinho, alegria e tornar essa data ainda mais inesquecível", diz parte da postagem.

Menino ganhou surpresa dos bombeiros de Xapuri — Foto: Eduarda Crisly/Arquivo pessoal

Ao g1 , a mãe de José, Eduarda Crisly, contou que o filho gosta muito da polícia e dos bombeiros. Diariamente, quando vai para a escola, José passa ao quartel dos bombeiros e fica encantado com o trabalho dos militares.

Quando se aproximava a época da data do aniversário, Eduarda perguntou ao filho qual tema ele queria da festinha. José não pensou duas vezes e falou que queria dos bombeir ideia de convidar os bombeiros foi do próprio aniversariante.

"Ele falou que queria convidar os bombeiros. Falei: 'Muito bem, vamos convidar'. Fui no quartel, contei para eles e perguntei se tinha como eles irem. Pediram meu contato e no dia falaram que estavam a caminho da festa, que era para aguardar na frente ", recordou.

Ainda segundo Eduarda, os bombeiros aceitaram o convite, contudo, ela não contou para o filho que os militares apareceriam. A mãe mandou fazer painel, doces, lembrancinhas, brigadeiros e bolo com a temática dos bombeiros.

E o José ganhou até farda dos bombeiros para usar na festa. "Ele que pediu. Dei várias opções e ele escolheu o bombeiro. Ele ficou ficou realizado, todo dia fala nesse aniversário dos bombeiros dele. Chegaram com a sirene ligada, foram muito solícitos, tiraram fotos e permaneceram no aniversário", disse Eduarda.

A mãe recorda também que o filho não largou mais os militares durante a festinha. "Ele cantou parabéns no colo dos bombeiros, ficou bem íntimo dos bombeiros", brincou.

Mãe de José Ravi mandou fazer uma 'farda' para eles dos bombeiros para o aniversário — Foto: Eduarda Crisly/Arquivo pessoal

Um dos presentes que José ganhou de aniversário foi um caminhão do Corpo de Bombeiros, segundo Eduarda.

"A tia dele perguntou o que ele queria ganhar. Ele disse que queria um caminhão dos bombeiros. Fizemos uma festinha simples, só para os de casa, mas bem aconchegante e muito especial. Ele aproveitou muito, brincou bastante com os primos e ficou feliz da vida", destacou.

O soldado France Willian fez parte da equipe que participou do aniversário de José. Ele destacou a importância da ação e disse que a admiração das criança é muito importante.

"Para mim é um sentimento muito verdadeiro. Para elas, o bombeiro representa coragem, proteção e esperança. O brilho nos olhos e os sorrisos ao se aproximarem dos militares demonstram o quanto essa profissão inspira e desperta sonhos. Eu acredito que o Bombeiro Militar também tem a missão de inspirar gerações, mostrando às crianças que servir ao próximo é um dos gestos mais nobres de humanidade", explicou.

articles.title: Horário do Enem em Rondônia: veja que horas fecham os portões | G1
articles.standfirst: Primeira etapa será aplicada neste domingo (8), e a segunda, no dia 15 de novembro. Estado tem uma hora a menos em relação a Brasília.
articles.summary: Primeira etapa será aplicada neste domingo (8), e a segunda, no dia 15 de novembro. Estado tem uma hora a menos em relação a Brasília.
articles.body:
Rondônia tem 43.682 inscritos no Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) 2026. A primeira etapa das provas será aplicada neste domingo (8), e a segunda, no dia 15 de novembro. Os candidatos devem ficar atentos ao fuso horário: o estado tem uma hora a menos em relação a Brasília.

No horário de Rondônia, os portões abrem às 11h e fecham ao meio-dia. As provas começam às 12h30. Como o Enem segue o horário de Brasília, os candidatos precisam considerar o horário local para não perder o exame.

Segundo o governo de Rondônia, dos 43.682 inscritos no estado, 30.679 são isentos da taxa de inscrição e 13.003 pagaram para participar. Em todo o país, o exame reúne mais de 5 milhões de candidatos.

No primeiro dia de provas, os participantes respondem às questões de Linguagens e Ciências Humanas e fazem a redação. O exame termina às 18h, no horário de Rondônia.

No segundo domingo (15), os horários de abertura e fechamento dos portões serão os mesmos. Os candidatos farão as provas de Matemática e Ciências da Natureza. O exame termina às 17h30, também no horário local.

O Cartão de Confirmação de Inscrição, que informa o local de prova, está disponível na Página do Participante.

A recomendação é que os candidatos acompanhem as orientações do Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (Inep) para evitar imprevistos.

Nesta reta final, os estudantes podem utilizar recursos digitais gratuitos do Ministério da Educação (MEC). O aplicativo MEC Enem oferece simulados interativos, banco de exercícios, videoaulas e orientações para a redação.

Plataformas como o MEC Idiomas e o MEC Livros oferecem cursos e bibliotecas digitais, enquanto o portal Guia do Enem reúne dicas e respostas para dúvidas frequentes.

O Enem é a principal porta de entrada para a educação superior no Brasil. As notas podem ser utilizadas no Sistema de Seleção Unificada (Sisu), no Programa Universidade para Todos (Prouni) e no Fundo de Financiamento Estudantil (Fies).

O resultado também é aceito em processos seletivos próprios de universidades e faculdades brasileiras, além de instituições de ensino em Portugal.

articles.title: Will the US resume its attacks on Iran?
articles.summary: Tehran says it’s ready with a maximum deterrence plan.
articles.body:
“Our response will be without geographical restrictions.”

That’s the warning from Iran as fears grow that the United States could renew all-out war after US President Donald Trump warned his country could attack Iran once US midterm elections were over.

Trump’s Republican Party suffered a severe blow in the congressional elections, losing its majority in both the House and the Senate. And Trump has conceded that the US-Israel war with Iran was partly to blame.

With the region on edge again, mediators have been trying to bring Tehran and Washington closer to a peace deal. But what will it take?

articles.title: Os fatores da 'onda azul', que deu aos democratas vitória histórica | G1
articles.standfirst: Democratas, de oposição a Donald Trump, retomaram o controle da Câmara dos Deputados e do Senado dos Estados Unidos. Resultado foi devido a uma conjunção de fatores, desde a rejeição a Trump, reflexos da guerra no bolso dos cidadãos e democratas carismáticos.
articles.summary: Uma espécie de tempestade perfeita está na raiz da vitória histórica conquistada pelo Partido Democrata, de oposição a Donald Trump, nas chamadas midterms.
articles.body:
Uma espécie de tempestade perfeita está na raiz da vitória histórica conquistada pelo Partido Democrata , de oposição a Donald Trump, nas chamadas midterms, eleições realizadas na terça-feira (3) nos Estados Unidos.

Desde o voto de protesto contra Trump até a alta nos votos antecipados, passando por uma nova leva de democratas carismáticos, a chamada "onda azul" — em referência à cor do Partido Democrata — foi proporcionada por uma combinação de fatores.

➡️ No pleito, feito para renovar parte do Legislativo e de governos estaduais, os democratas recuperaram o controle tanto da Câmara dos Deputados quanto do Senado, que eram controlados pelo Partido Republicano, de Trump, desde que ele voltou à Casa Branca, em janeiro de 2025.

É praxe, na política norte-americana, que o partido de oposição ao presidente ganhe o controle de pelo menos uma das Casas nas midterms. Desta vez, no entanto, os democratas avançaram sobre cadeiras historicamente ocupadas por republicanos .

Também haviam conquistado, até a última atualização desta reportagem, 28 governos estaduais, incluindo os de redutos históricos republicanos, como o Texas e o Kansas.

Veja, abaixo, fatores que levaram à vitória democrata:

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, tira o chapéu por um instante ao sair do espelho d'água do Lincoln Memorial, após sua reabertura depois de meses de reformas, em Washington, DC, EUA, em 2 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Umit Bektas TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY

Um levantamento feito pela agência de notícias norte-americana Associated Press (AP), que ouviu mais de 100 mil eleitores em todos os 50 estados dos EUA, apontou que cerca de 40% dos eleitores votaram para "expressar oposição" a Donald Trump.

Para o comentarista de política internacional da Globonews Marcelo Lins, os resultados foram, antes de tudo, um voto de protesto contra o presidente dos EUA. "Donald Trump prometeu entregar uma economia estável, não colocar os Estados Unidos em conflitos e trazer militares para casa", afirmou.

"Ele não entregou nada disso. Entrega uma inflação pressionada. O desemprego não é uma preocupação neste momento, mas as guerras sem fim são outra preocupação. Exaurem os cofres dos Estados Unidos. E, claro, o preço do petróleo, que não deixa os americanos se planejarem nem para o curto, muito menos para o medio e longo prazos".

O professor de Relações Internacionais da Universidade Federal Fluminense (UFF) Vitélio Brustolin disse achar que o voto de rejeição foi o fator-chave do êxito democrata. "As pessoas foram às urnas por conta da insatisfação", afirmou o professor ao g1 .

As últimas pesquisas de aprovação do governo de Donald Trump já indicavam que os resultados a favor do Partido Democrata poderiam ser mais expressivos. A popularidade do presidente norte-americano vinha despencando nos últimos meses e, em outubro, a semanas das midterms, alcançou a baixa histórica de 31% de aprovação da população .

A popularidade em baixa não permitiu que Trump mobilizasse seus eleitores, mesmo com o presidente pedindo que eles votassem como se ele próprio estivesse nas urnas.

Veículos passam por um outdoor com uma imagem do Estreito de Ormuz e com os lábios costurados do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, em uma praça no centro de Teerã, Irã, sábado, 2 de maio de 2026. — Foto: AP Photo/Vahid Salemi

A guerra no Irã também encabeça a lista de fatores que entregaram a vitória aos democratas. Traumatizados com conflitos como os do Vietnã, norte-americanos digeriram mal a demora de Trump em dar um fim à guerra que ainda trava contra o Irã.

Mas pesou mais o fato de que o conflito vem mexendo no bolso dos norte-americanos. A alta no petróleo provocada pelo conflito iniciado pelo presidente dos EUA encareceu ainda mais o custo de vida no país , que já era alto.

O próprio vice-presidente dos EUA, JD Vance, em sua primeira manifestação após os resultados, culpou o conflito .

"A razão pela qual perdemos é a guerra. O próprio presidente disse isso na noite passada. Se você quiser argumentar que valeu a pena, que perder o Senado pelos próximos 6 anos valeu a pena, então faça isso. Argumente que foi um custo válido a pagar. Mas todo mundo sabe por que perdemos", disse Vance.

O candidato democrata ao Senado pelo Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed, atrás de uma bandeira dos Estados Unidos em ato de campanha em Mount Clemens, no Michigan, em 31 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/ AP

Ao lado da insatisfação com Trump, sua "guerra sem fim" e a economia, uma nova leva de candidatos democratas, mais carismáticos e com mais apelo que nomes do partido em pleitos anteriores, mobilizou o eleitorado.

Encabeçaram essa lista o candidato ao Senado pelo Texas, James Talarico , o candidato ao Senado pelo Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed , e o senador pela Georgia, Jon Ossof . Os três foram eleitos nas midterms.

Com linguagem afiada e mais capacidade de mobilização pelas redes sociais, esses candidatos conseguiram ajudar os democratas a recuperar terreno e fazer com que eleitores voltassem a levantar a bandeira do partido, um movimento encabeçado pelo prefeito de Nova York, Zohran Mamdani.

"Ele despertou algo nos eleitores", disse à rede de TV ABC News a cientista política Christina Greer, da Universidade Fordham. "Antes, os eleitores achavam que precisavam aceitar o 'status quo' da política tradicional".

Embora não haja um grande nome forte atualmente no Partido Democrata, a sigla conseguiu mobilizar candidatos carismáticos em regiões relevantes e até em redutos republicanos, como o Texas e o Kansas.

A mobilização pelo voto antecipado, um comportamento tradicionalmente democrata, foi um fator decisivo neste pleito. Quase 59 milhões de americanos votaram antes do dia da votação, contra 45,9 milhões nas midterms de 2022, segundo o levantamento da AP.

Pesquisas revelaram que, de fato, houve uma forte mobilização de eleitores democratas para o voto antecipado.

Um levantamento do site de notícias Axios mostrou ainda que o voto antecipado foi especialmente forte entre eleitores negros e latino-americanos, grupos que penderam para o Partido Democrata neste pleito.

Separados pelo ICE é o nome da fotografia tirada por Carol Guzy e vencedora do prêmio Imagem do Ano de 2026 do World Press Photo. — Foto: Carol Guzy/ZUMA Press, iWitness para Miami Herald/World Press Photo 2026 via BBC

Tradicionalmente democrata , o eleitorado latino-americano — que inflou e hoje representa mais de 15% de todos os eleitores do país — havia se aproximado do Partido Republicano nas últimas eleições, em 2020.

Na ocasião, esse eleitorado expressava mais confiança em Donald Trump para retomar a economia do país e descolava-se do discurso anti-imigração de Trump, que eles enxergavam como direcionado a novos imigrantes, distantes de latino-americanos que vivem há anos ou décadas nos EUA.

No entanto, além de a economia não melhorar, a dura política anti-imigração de Trump não caiu bem entre os latino-americanos, que acabaram afetados direta ou indiretamente pela caça de agentes ICE a estrangeiros.

A resposta veio nas urnas. O levantamento feito pela AP revelou que, entre os eleitores latino-americanos, o apoio aos candidatos republicanos foi menor que o registrado por Trump dois anos atrás .

De acordo com a pesquisa, seis em cada 10 eleitores hispânicos declararam ter votado no Partido Democrata — na eleição presidencial de 2024, esse grupo ficou praticamente dividido entre Donald Trump e a candidata democrata Kamala Harris, segundo o AP VoteCast.

A pesquisa feita pela Associated Press também revelou uma guinada acentuada dos eleitores jovens em direção à esquerda . Sete em cada 10 eleitores com menos de 30 anos disseram ter votado em candidatos democratas para Câmara dos Deputados.

O desempenho dos candidatos democratas entre os eleitores com menos de 30 anos foi maior que o apoio que esse grupo conferiu à vice-presidente Kamala Harris, que disputou a presidência com Donald Trump.

A maioria dos eleitores com menos de 30 anos, ainda de acordo com a pesquisa, afirmou ter votado para expressar oposição ao atual presidente .

O ex-presidente dos EUA, Barack Obama, faz campanha com o candidato democrata ao Senado dos EUA, Abdul El- Sayed , e a candidata democrata ao governo, Jocelyn Benson, em Detroit, Michigan — Foto: REUTERS/Rebecca Cook

Afastado de grandes comícios, o ex-presidente Barack Obama foi um reforço de peso para os democratas na reta final das eleições de meio de mandato.

Quase uma década depois de deixar a Casa Branca, ele voltou aos palanques para mobilizar eleitores em estados estratégicos, como Ohio, Michigan e Geórgia. A capacidade de Obama atrair atenção e entusiasmar a base democrata foi destacada pela imprensa norte-americana como um dos principais mobilizadores do partido.

O ex-presidente dividiu o palco com o candidato ao Senado por Ohio, Sherrod Brown, a candidata ao governo do estado, Amy Acton, com o senador Jon Ossoff e com a candidata democrata ao governo da Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms, que se tornou a primeira mulher negra a se eleger governadora de um estado americano.

Mas o destaque foram os atos de Obama ao lado de Abdul El-Sayed ( veja na imagem acima ).

articles.title: Donald Trump avalia resultado das midterms e cita poder de veto | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente dos Estados Unidos fez sua primeira aparição pública após derrota do Partido Republicano nas eleições de meio de mandato; polítco citou alta da gasolina como um dos fatores que explicam o desempenho da legenda.
articles.summary: Donald Trump avalia as midterms, justifica a alta da gasolina pela guerra no Irã e afirma que usará o poder de veto caso os democratas tentem ser destrutivos.
articles.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmou que a guerra contra o Irã contribuiu para a derroda do partido Republicano nas midterms, eleições de meio de mandato que definem a Câmara e parte do Senado. A declaração foi dada em conversa com jornalistas nesta quarta-feira (4).

O presidente dos EUA concordou com seu vice, J.D. Vance, sobre a culpa do conflito no resultado das eleições. "Bem, acho que isso é em grande parte verdade, porque fez a gasolina subir um pouco no curto prazo, e provavelmente é verdade. Mas, ao mesmo tempo, se eu tivesse que fazer de novo, eu teria que fazer de novo, porque, a longo prazo, é a única resposta. Não se pode deixar o Irã ter uma arma nuclear".

Questionado se o ataque ao Irã valeu a pena, respondeu que sim. "Bem, não há escolha... Tem que ser feito. Não se pode deixar o Irã ter uma arma nuclear, ou tudo o que vocês veem aqui pode, um dia, deixar de existir.”

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, discursa no dia em que a última viga de aço é instalada no salão de baile da Casa Branca, em Washington — Foto: REUTERS/Evan Vucci

Trump também afirmou que "provavelmente se dará bem" com os democratas, mas lembrou que possui poder de veto.

"Provavelmente vou me dar bem com os democratas, a menos que queiram ser destrutivos, mas nós temos poder de veto. Então, se não gostarmos do que estão fazendo...", declarou Trump. "Eles já ligaram e querem conversar sobre as coisas, e tudo bem".

O Partido Democrata, que faz oposição a Trump, conquistou maioria na Câmara e no Senado.

Após os primeiros resultados negativos para seu partido, Trump publicou a foto de um boné vermelho com a palavra “veto”. Dias antes, o presidente antecipou como agiria caso os democratas vencessem as eleições.

"Acho que vou me tornar o Sr. Veto", disse o presidente ao podcast "Pod Force One", do "New York Post". "Eles vão enviar algumas coisas. Você veta. E, eventualmente, depois de um ou dois meses sendo vetados, eles só estão perdendo tempo, vêm até nós e fazemos um acordo."

Nas redes sociais, Trump posta foto de um foto com a palavra 'veto'. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Na conversa com jornalistas, Trump voltou a insistir que, se seu nome estivesse nas cédulas, ele teria ganhado. "Vocês viram as pessoas, lotando os comícios, milhares e milhares de pessoas em todos os comícios."

Essa foi a primeira aparição pública de Trump depois dos resultados das midterms. Segundo a Reuters, o presidente convocou a imprensa ao canteiro de obras da Casa Branca para falar sobre o salão de baile que encomendou.

“Será o salão de baile mais bonito, eu acho, de qualquer lugar do mundo”, disse Trump de pé diante da última viga de aço do projeto, que havia sido assinada pelos operários da obra. Depois de falar, Trump também assinou a viga.

A guerra contra o Irã, iniciada por EUA e Israel em 28 de fevereiro, provocou uma disparada nos preços dos combustíveis, nas passagens aéreas e na inflação geral. Estimativas apontam que a guerra custou o equivalente a até US$ 100 bilhões (cerca de R$ 508 bilhões) aos cofres americanos, segundo fontes do Pentágono.

Uma pesquisa da Reuters/Ipsos na véspera das midterms mostrou que cerca de 48% dos eleitores americanos apontaram o custo de vida como a principal questão na hora de votar nas eleições de meio de mandato.

Além disso, apenas 25% dos eleitores consideram que a ação militar valeu o custo, enquanto 55% dizem que não valeu. Outros 18% não tinham certeza.

Trump argumentou que a guerra era necessária para impedir que o Irã desenvolvesse armas nucleares e, após os ataques, chegou a afirmar que o conflito acabaria rapidamente. Após meses de declarações contraditórias e de um acordo de cessar-fogo fracassado, a guerra continua, mas em menor intensidade.

O ataque mais recente dos Estados Unidos teria sido na última segunda-feira (2) contra a ilha iraniana de Qeshm , segundo informou o jornal The Wall Street Journal, citando autoridades americanas.

articles.title: Doença de Newcastle: SC confirma 4º foco em menos de um mês  | G1
articles.standfirst: Novo foco foi confimado em Nova Erechim, dentro da área de emergência zoosanitária. Após confirmação do vírus em 18 de outubro, vários países suspenderam produtos da avicultura brasileira.
articles.summary: Novo foco foi confimado em Nova Erechim, dentro da área de emergência zoosanitária. Após confirmação do vírus em 18 de outubro, vários países suspenderam produtos da avicultura brasileira.
articles.body:
O Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária (Mapa) confirmou um novo foco da doença de Newcastle em uma propriedade avícola de Nova Erechim , no Oeste de Santa Catarina .

A identificação foi divulgada na terça-feira (3), e representa a quarta ocorrência registrada no estado desde a declaração de emergência zoossanitária.

A doença causa, desde 18 de outubro , restrições à exportação de produtos da avicultura brasileira .

Segundo o ministério, o novo caso foi identificado durante ações de vigilância realizadas na área de restrição já estabelecida.

A propriedade está localizada dentro desse perímetro, delimitado após as primeiras confirmações da doença.

Fiscalização agropecuária da Cidasc contra a doença de Newcastle — Foto: Kelly Magri/Cidasc

🔍 🐔 A doença de Newcastle é uma enfermidade viral que contamina aves domésticas e silvestres, podendo ser letal para esses animais. Em humanos, ela pode causar, no máximo, conjuntivite transitória, que costuma durar cerca de uma semana. A transmissão ocorre pelo contato, e não pelo consumo.

O Serviço Veterinário Oficial deve adotar os protocolos previstos para emergências zoossanitárias, que incluem investigação epidemiológica , ações de vigilância e medidas para conter a disseminação do vírus .

Os três primeiros focos foram confirmados nos municípios de Nova Itaberaba , Coronel Freitas e Nova Erechim. Nessas propriedades, todas as medidas previstas nos protocolos de resposta já foram adotadas, e os locais se encontram em vazio sanitário.

Em nota, o Mapa informou que continua atuando em conjunto com os órgãos estaduais de defesa agropecuária para controlar a ocorrência e proteger a avicultura nacional.

articles.title: Jacareí reavalia valores de imóveis em 18 regiões e pode elevar IPTU 2027; entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Códigos de referência tiveram aumentos de até 650%, mas o impacto no valor final do IPTU de 2027 ainda está sendo calculado pela Prefeitura.
articles.summary: Códigos de referência tiveram aumentos de até 650%, mas o impacto no valor final do IPTU de 2027 ainda está sendo calculado pela Prefeitura.
articles.body:
A Prefeitura de Jacareí atualizou os valores de referência de imóveis em 18 regiões da cidade. Em alguns locais, os códigos utilizados para classificar os terrenos e as edificações tiveram aumentos de até 650%.

A mudança pode impactar o cálculo do Imposto Predial e Territorial Urbano (IPTU) a partir de 2027. O percentual de aumento do imposto, no entanto, ainda não foi definido.

A revisão foi estabelecida por meio de um decreto publicado na última semana e altera parcialmente a Planta Genérica de Valores (PGV) do município.

Segundo o secretário de Meio Ambiente e Planejamento Urbano, Rogério Costa Manso, a última atualização havia sido feita em 2013. Desde então, a cidade passou por mudanças na infraestrutura e expansão de loteamentos, o que motivou a reavaliação.

O trabalho começou a ser preparado no ano passado, quando a prefeitura contratou uma empresa para fazer imagens aéreas do município e analisar o crescimento da cidade.

Nesta etapa, 18 regiões foram reclassificadas. A análise levou em consideração mudanças como a presença de escolas, unidades de saúde, iluminação pública e redes de água e esgoto.

Cidade de Jacareí — Foto: Divulgaçã/Prefeitura de Jacareí

Entre as áreas residenciais, os três maiores aumentos nos valores de referência foram registrados no Residencial Villa Europa e na Avenida Nicola Capucci, no Parque Vale dos Lagos, e no Residencial Fogaça.

Já entre as áreas comerciais e industriais, os maiores reajustes ocorreram na R odovia Geraldo Scavone, na Estrada Soldab e na Rodovia Dom Pedro. De acordo com a Prefeitura, as mudanças atingirão cerca de 2% das propriedades da cidade.

A Prefeitura ainda não sabe informar qual será o impacto da revisão no valor final do IPTU. Segundo o secretário, o estudo foi encaminhado à Secretaria de Finanças, responsável por calcular os efeitos da mudança para os contribuintes e para a arrecadação municipal.

A expectativa é que os novos valores sejam conhecidos com o lançamento dos carnês do IPTU de 2027, previsto para o fim de dezembro ou início de janeiro.

O secretário também explicou que o imposto passa por uma atualização anual pela inflação. Ainda não foi possível, porém, calcular quanto a reclassificação dos imóveis poderá representar além dessa correção.

articles.title: Compra planejada: Saiba como organizar as finanças para realizar sonhos | G1
articles.standfirst: Escolhas financeiras conscientes são essenciais para transformar planos em realidade.
articles.summary: Escolhas financeiras conscientes são essenciais para transformar planos em realidade.
articles.body:
Sonhar não custa nada, mas transformar planos em realidade tem seu preço. Seja para conquistar a casa própria, trocar de carro ou fazer uma viagem desejada, o caminho entre o desejo e a conquista passa pelo bolso. E, para que os planos não fiquem apenas no papel, o primeiro passo é organizar as finanças e buscar alternativas que ajudem a realizar esses objetivos sem deixar o orçamento pelo caminho.

Emanuelle Siqueira de Azevedo, gerente da agência do Sicoob em São Francisco de Itabapoana, no Norte Fluminense — Foto: Divulgação

Para Emanuelle Siqueira de Azevedo, gerente da agência do Sicoob em São Francisco de Itabapoana, no Norte Fluminense, o planejamento e a organização financeira são fundamentais para entender o que cabe no orçamento e idealizar um sonho, sem comprometer as despesas essenciais do dia a dia.

“Conhecer a própria realidade financeira é fundamental, separando as despesas fixas das variáveis e colocando na ponta do lápis quanto é o ganho e o gasto mensal. Esse cuidado ajuda a identificar gastos desnecessários, que podem ser reduzidos e transformados em economias significativas. Com metas definidas, organização e constância, os sonhos ficam cada vez mais próximos da realidade”, explicou.

Emanuelle Siqueira de Azevedo, gerente da agência do Sicoob — Foto: Divulgação

Segundo a gerente do Sicoob, um erro comum das pessoas durante o planejamento é assumir compromissos financeiros extras, o que pode dificultar, atrasar ou até mesmo impedir que se chegue a um objetivo definido inicialmente.

“É importante evitar decisões por impulso, que possam comprometer o orçamento. Do nada, a pessoa assume um parcelamento, por exemplo. Embora o valor aparentemente seja baixo, o custo total do produto ou serviço adquirido gera um impacto na renda”, disse.

Para quem busca por realizações pessoais, a educação financeira pode ser um fator de grande diferença durante o planejamento. Nesse cenário, o Sicoob auxilia seus cooperados, por meio de um time de especialistas, em um trabalho que vai muito além da apresentação de um produto, mas que, de fato, entende a necessidade do associado e sua realidade financeira para discernir as soluções mais adequadas.

“Temos linhas de crédito, investimento, poupança e outros produtos. Porém, antes de indicar qualquer uma delas, através do nosso relacionamento com o cooperado, fazemos uma análise e orientamos de forma personalizada, buscando uma solução que faça diferença e sentido na vida dessa pessoa”, contou Emanuelle.

Para quem não tem urgência em adquirir um bem e consegue se planejar para esperar a contemplação, o consórcio é uma das alternativas mais indicadas. Sem juros de financiamento, essa modalidade não se limita aos investimentos em veículos, mas alcança também possibilidades de investimento em energia solar para casa, móveis planejados, viagens e até mesmo procedimentos estéticos.

“Não existe uma opção que seja a melhor para todo mundo. Depende muito da necessidade de cada associado. Enquanto na contratação de crédito, o bem é imediato, porém, com juros na operação, o consórcio pode oferecer recursos que as pessoas nem imaginam. Recentemente, uma associada fez uma carta de crédito para a tão sonhada cirurgia plástica. Logo depois, conseguiu alcançar o carro e, agora, a cirurgia da filha. No consórcio, trabalhamos especificamente com o sonho das pessoas”, destacou a gerente.

Agência do Sicoob em São Francisco de Itabapoana, no Norte Fluminense — Foto: Ass. comunicação Sicoob ES

O Sicoob reúne mais de 10,6 milhões de cooperados e está presente em todos os estados brasileiros e no Distrito Federal. O sistema regional Sicoob ES reúne 217 pontos de atendimento, mais de 1,1 milhão de cooperados e atuação no Espírito Santo, Rio de Janeiro, Bahia (nas cidades de Salvador, Lauro de Freitas, Ilhéus, Itabuna e Santa Luzia), além de São José dos Campos (SP). articles.title: VÍDEO: Cozinheira é lançada de moto após passar por quebra-molas | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a família, a estrutura foi construída recentemente e ainda não possui pintura ou placas de alerta. A Strans informou que a sinalização deve ser concluída nesta semana.
articles.summary: Segundo a família, a estrutura foi construída recentemente e ainda não possui pintura ou placas de alerta. A Strans informou que a sinalização deve ser concluída nesta semana.
articles.body:
A cozinheira Verônica da Silva ficou ferida após ser arremessada da motocicleta que pilotava, ao passar por um quebra-mola, na manhã desta quarta-feira (4), na Avenida Hugo Bastos, no bairro Vale Quem Tem, Zona Leste de Teresina .

Em entrevista à Rede Clube, a filha dela, Zilda Vitória Felix, informou que Verônica seguia para o trabalho no momento do acidente. Ela alegou que o quebra-molas foi construído recentemente e que o local não possui sinalização adequada. Veja a nota completa.

Em nota, a Superintendência Municipal de Transportes e Trânsito (Strans) informou que as equipes estão finalizando as obras e ainda restam a pintura e a sinalização do quebra-molas. A previsão é que o serviço seja concluído ainda nesta semana.

"Não tem nenhuma sinalização, não tem nenhuma placa. Inclusive, o quebra-molas é do tamanho da calçada e tem a mesma cor do asfalto", afirmou a filha.

Imagens de câmeras de segurança registraram o momento em que a cozinheira passa pelo quebra-molas e cai. É possível ver ainda que a motocicleta gira no ar e que a mulher arrasta o rosto no asfalto. Em seguida, ela senta na pista.

Cozinheira é arremessada de moto após passar por quebra-molas sem sinalização em Teresina — Foto: Reprodução

Cerca de seis minutos antes, as câmeras também registraram a passagem de um ônibus pela via. Nas imagens, o veículo balança fortemente ao passar pelo quebra-molas e permanece parado por alguns segundos logo em seguida.

Segundo Zilda, a mãe foi levada ao Hospital de Urgência de Teresina (HUT) com diversos ferimentos e cortes. Ela explicou que Verônica tem hérnias de disco e um pino na coluna, condições que teriam sido agravadas pela queda.

A filha afirmou ainda que a mãe não ficou internada, mas precisou realizar diversos exames e pode precisar se afastar do trabalho durante a recuperação.

"Infelizmente, os médicos disseram que talvez ela nem consiga retornar ao trabalho, justamente por causa dessa queda", lamentou.

A Superintendência Municipal de Transportes e Trânsito (Strans) informa que as equipes de engenharia estão finalizando os serviços nas faixas elevadas da capital. A primeira etapa já foi concluída, restando a pintura e a sinalização.

Devido às chuvas registradas na semana passada, foi necessário reajustar o cronograma, uma vez que o serviço exige um intervalo mínimo de dois dias de secagem do asfalto antes da pintura.

A Strans informa que os serviços de sinalização serão realizados ainda esta semana, garantindo melhores condições de segurança para pedestres e condutores.

articles.title: Titanic's unsinkable stoker's watch sells for nearly £4k
articles.summary: A pocket watch belonging to a survivor of the Titanic has been sold at auction in Cheltenham.
articles.body:
A pocket watch belonging to a stoker who survived four shipwrecks, including the Titanic and its sister ship Britannic, has sold at auction for nearly £4,000.

The watch was gifted to Arthur John Priest who was nicknamed the "unsinkable" stoker after he survived the sinking of four ships in just five years.

Described as "quite a rare, amazing find", Bespoke Auctions' senior auctioneer Nicholas Granger said the watch had attracted quite a lot of interest from prospective buyers ahead of the auction.

With a starting bid of £3,000, it went under the hammer at Sudeley Castle in Cheltenham, Gloucestershire and was sold for £3,800.

New theatre centre 'vitally important', says actor

Home births to resume as maternity unit to reopen

Lost WW1 record tells unique stories of servicemen

According to accounts of his life, John Priest worked his entire life as a member of the so-called "black gang", shovelling coal in the boiler rooms of steam-powered ships.

Between 1912 and 1917, he survived multiple sinkings including the RMS Titanic in 1912, RMS Alcantara in 1916, HMHS Britannic in 1916 and SS Donegal in 1917.

When the Titanic sank he was in the bowels of the ship but despite the odds of surviving being against him, he was rescued from the sea suffering from frostbitten toes and an injured leg.

The inscription on the pocket watch suggests it was presented to Priest as a thank you for saving the life of a man when the Britannic sank after striking a mine in the Aegean Sea in 1916.

A year later, after sustaining a head injury when SS Donegal sank in 1917, Priest retired from his life at sea and died in Southampton on 11 February 1937.

"He got a bit of a name for himself as the unlucky sailor, and some people actually didn't want to sail with him in the end," said Granger.

"Auctioneering is a bit like a treasure hunt, and when these things come along, it's amazing the amount of interest we get, because these are parts of history."

Priest's watch is not the only object at the auction that survived the Titanic - a silver cigarette case, recovered from the body of a steward on board, sold for £5,700.

articles.title: How Democrats clawed back support from five key voter groups in US midterms
articles.summary: Democrats had a sweeping victory during the 2026 US midterm elections, bringing focus to some of the key demographics where they made significant gains.
articles.body: Democrats had a sweeping victory during the 2026 US midterm elections, bringing focus to some of the key demographics where they made significant gains. Thereby, reversing several advances president Donald Trump made among traditionally Democratic voters in the 2024 presidential race, according to the AP Voter Poll.A survey of more than 100,000 voters across all 50 states found that voters under 30, Hispanic voters, Black voters, moderates and lower-income households shifted towards Democratic candidates, helping the party secure victories in several key races.Young voters recorded one of the sharpest swingsNearly 7 in 10 voters under 30 said they supported the Democratic candidate in their local House race, compared with roughly 3 in 10 who backed Republicans. During the 2024 presidential elections the voters were equally divided between Kamala and Trump.First-time midterm voters, who tend to be younger, also largely favoured Democrats. However, voters under 30 accounted for only about one in 10 of the electorate, limiting the overall impact of the shift. Their dissatisfaction with the country's direction was evident, with about half saying they were angry about the state of affairs. Nearly 6 in 10 also said opposing Trump was one reason for their House vote.The Democratic shift among younger voters was visible in all five Senate races where the party gained seats — Texas, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio and North Carolina.Hispanic voters move back towards DemocratsRepublicans appeared to lose most, if not all, of the gains Trump made among Hispanic voters in 2024. About 6 in 10 Hispanic voters backed Democratic candidates in their local House races, while roughly one-third supported Republicans. This compared with around 4 in 10 Hispanic voters who had backed Trump in the 2024 presidential election.The shift was particularly evident in Texas, where Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton in the Senate race. Roughly 6 in 10 Hispanic voters supported Talarico, compared with about 3 in 10 who voted for Paxton.In Florida, Republican Senator Ashley Moody managed to narrowly secure re-election, but received support from fewer than half of Hispanic voters.Trump's gains among Black voters prove short-livedBlack voters also moved back towards Democrats after Trump's gains in the previous presidential election.Only about 1 in 10 Black men supported the Republican candidate in their local House race, down from roughly one-quarter who had backed Trump in 2024. Around 9 in 10 Black voters supported Democratic House candidates, compared with approximately 8 in 10 who voted for Harris.The shift was particularly pronounced in Georgia, where Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor. About 9 in 10 Black men supported Bottoms, compared with roughly three-quarters who had backed Harris in 2024. Support among Black women remained around 9 in 10.In Florida, however, Republican Byron Donalds, elected the state's first Black governor, did not secure comparable support. About one-quarter of Black men voted for him over Democrat David Jolly, while only around 1 in 10 Black women backed the Republican.Moderates give Democrats an edgeDemocrats also strengthened their position among moderate voters, a group that proved particularly important in Senate races where the party flipped Republican-held seats.Around two-thirds of moderates supported Democratic candidates in their local House races, up from approximately 6 in 10 who had backed Harris in 2024.The poll found that roughly 8 in 10 moderates believed Congress was not doing enough to provide checks and balances on the presidency. A similar proportion reported experiencing at least moderate financial hardship because of inflation over the past year.Moderate voters were a significant part of Democratic victories in several closely contested Senate races. In Kansas, Democrat Adam Hamilton won roughly 7 in 10 moderate voters, compared with around half who supported Harris in 2024. In Iowa, Josh Turek secured about two-thirds of moderates, while Roy Cooper won roughly three-quarters of the group in North Carolina.Lower-income voters turn towards Democrats amid cost concernsEconomic pressures also appear to have influenced the shift, with lower-income voters moving towards Democrats amid concerns over the rising cost of living.More than half of voters whose household income was below $50,000 in 2025 backed Democratic candidates in their local House races. In 2024, this group had been almost evenly divided between Trump and Harris. Around 3 in 10 US voters reported an annual household income below $50,000.These voters were more likely than higher-income groups to express concern over food and grocery prices, fuel costs and utility bills. About 6 in 10 voters earning less than $50,000 said the cost of living was crucial to their voting decision, compared with roughly half of those earning more.The AP Voter Poll was conducted by SSRS for The Associated Press, ABC News, CBS News, CNN, Fox News Media, NBC News and Versant. It surveyed more than 100,000 registered voters across all 50 states between October 19 and November 3 in Alaska, and October 22 and November 3 in other states. articles.title: Michigan neighbours built a boardwalk and dock believing they could share lake access, but never signed an easement; after new owners blocked the route, a court upheld $55,750 for improvements on land they did not own
articles.summary: Sharing access to a lakefront can seem like a straightforward arrangement between neighbours, particularly when both families contribute money and effort
articles.body: Sharing access to a lakefront can seem like a straightforward arrangement between neighbours, particularly when both families contribute money and effort to build facilities. But an informal understanding can become a costly property dispute when ownership changes and the new owners refuse to honour the arrangement. In Michigan, a couple who helped build a boardwalk and dock believing they could use them to reach a lake found themselves without a legally enforceable easement after the neighbouring property was sold.In its October 28, 2026, unpublished decision in Jeremy Leffring v. Mark Cahill, available on Justia, the Michigan Court of Appeals upheld a $55,750 award to the couple for improvements they had made to the neighbouring property. The court agreed that they had not established an enforceable easement because there was no written agreement. However, it found that they were entitled to compensation because they had not acted in bad faith when constructing and maintaining the boardwalk and dock. The appeals court also upheld the dismissal of the new owners' claim seeking indemnification from the previous owners.How the neighbours agreed to share lake accessThe dispute involved Jeremy and Ivanna Leffring, who owned a home near a lake in Michigan, and their neighbours, Timothy and Allison Updyke. The two families had an arrangement under which they shared access to the lake through a boardwalk and dock located on the Updykes' property. Both families mutually constructed the boardwalk and dock for shared use and contributed to maintaining the improvements, believing that the Leffrings could continue using the facilities to reach the water.However, the arrangement was never formalised through a written easement. An easement is a legal right that allows someone to use another person's property for a specific purpose, such as accessing a lake or crossing a neighbouring parcel. The Updykes eventually sold their property to Mark Cahill and Lindsey Bissett. The new owners initially allowed the Leffrings to continue using the boardwalk, but the relationship deteriorated in 2022.The conflict escalated after the Leffrings listed their home for sale and planned to lease it to tenants until the property was sold. Cahill and Bissett then installed a 'No Trespassing' sign along the boardwalk and placed a pile of sticks along the route used by the Leffrings, their family members and guests. The couple subsequently sought legal protection to continue accessing the lake.Why the court upheld the $55,750 compensationThe trial court concluded that the verbal arrangement did not create an enforceable easement because Michigan's statute of frauds required the agreement to be documented in writing. However, the court considered whether the Leffrings could receive compensation for the improvements they had made to the Updykes' property. Under Michigan Court Rule 3.411(F), a party who loses a claim to title to disputed property may seek compensation for the increase in the property's value resulting from buildings or improvements they made. However, compensation is not available if those improvements were made in bad faith.After a bench trial, the court found that the Leffrings had acted in good faith. They had mutually agreed with the previous owners to build and maintain the boardwalk and dock, shared the construction expenses and continued maintaining the facilities after the property changed hands. The new owners had also initially allowed them to use the facilities without objection and even helped with annual maintenance during their first year of ownership. The court therefore awarded the couple $55,750, representing their contribution to the increase in the value of the neighbouring property through the improvements.New owners' attempt to recover money from previous owners failsCahill and Bissett also argued that the Updykes should compensate them for the financial consequences of the dispute. They claimed that the previous owners had failed to disclose the claimed easement properly when selling the property. However, the Updykes had marked the existence of encroachments and easements as unknown in their disclosure statement while specifically mentioning that the dock was shared with the neighbour to the east.The appeals court found that the new owners could not simultaneously argue that no enforceable easement existed and claim compensation for the failure to disclose an easement that had no legal validity. It also rejected their argument for equitable indemnification, finding insufficient evidence that the Updykes had been unjustly enriched at their expense. The Michigan Court of Appeals affirmed the lower court's decision, leaving the $55,750 compensation award intact.The ruling highlights the financial risks of relying on informal property arrangements. Although the Leffrings could not secure a legal right to continue accessing the lake, the court recognised their good-faith investment in improvements that increased the value of land they did not own.You use AI every day. articles.title: British man infected with Ebola in DR Congo to be flown back to UK
articles.summary: The wider risk to the UK public from the deadly virus remains low, a government spokesperson says.
articles.body:
A British man who has tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo will be flown back to the UK.

It is the first confirmed case of a UK national contracting Ebola during the most recent outbreak of the rare but deadly virus in DR Congo, which has so far led to more than 5,000 deaths.

It is not clear when the flight will take place.

Earlier, a UK government spokesperson said there were "well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this" and that the risk to the public remains low.

Reuters news agency reported the infected man is a healthcare worker, citing an internal document BBC News has not seen.

Imported Ebola cases are extremely rare in the UK and have resulted in no deaths.

There have only been four confirmed cases of the virus in the UK - one, in 1976, resulting from a laboratory incident, and three involving health workers who were responding to an outbreak in West Africa between 2014 and 2015.

A UK government spokesperson said: "The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated.

"Further information will be shared in due course as appropriate. The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low."

There have been more than 10,000 confirmed cases since the recent outbreak in DR Congo started in May, which has grown to become the second most deadly recorded spate of infections, behind the outbreak in West Africa.

It has since become the deadliest in the country's history, with a fatality rate of 48.6% reported at the end of last month.

Ebola can result in serious illness and death. Early symptoms include vomiting and diarrhoea but it can progress to organ failure and internal bleeding.

The virus spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

The ongoing outbreak centred on DR Congo is fueled by the Bundibugyo variant of the virus.

There is no approved vaccine but the World Health Organisation said experts have recommended adding two new candidate drugs to an ongoing clinical trial.

The vaccines, one developed by the University of Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, and another by the firm Moderna, will join the trial once they are approved by Congolese health authorities.

It will be the first time jabs specifically designed to protect against the Bundibugyo virus are tested during an outbreak.

Since the outbreak, Ebola cases have also been confirmed in Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda.

articles.title: Palestinian citizens of Israel face intimidation after election success
articles.summary: After winning a record number of parliament seats, Palestinian-led parties face campaign against them.
articles.body:
Israel has officially certified its election results – delivering a blow to right-wing claims of a stolen vote – but the record 19 seats captured by Palestinian-led parties have triggered aggressive police raids, arbitrary arrests, and targeted interrogations by state security apparatuses.

The electoral gains made by the parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel – the Joint List and the United Arab List (Ra’am) – could give the Zionist opposition to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu the upper hand in forming the next government, if they choose to work with the Arab parties.

Meanwhile, Netanyahu and his allies have portrayed the increased vote share for the Palestinian-led parties as the result of illegality , a+nd say they represent Jewish Israelis.

Political analyst Mamoun Abu Amer told Al Jazeera that the political backlash was preplanned.

“From the beginning, it was clearly a systematic campaign when Arab citizens mobilised heavily, especially in the villages, the Naqab and the Bedouin areas,” Abu Amer said. He noted that the heavy turnout deeply shocked the Israeli political establishment, prompting Netanyahu to launch a smear campaign to discredit the democratic process.

Ahmad Tibi, leader of the Ta’al Party – which is part of the Joint List – shared a similar analysis.

“There is no indication that the elections were manipulated in the Arab towns, as everyone expected the voting rate to be high this time in advance due to the bad reality created by this government for our public,” Tibi told Al Jazeera. “On the contrary, there was a press report on Israel’s Channel 12 television revealing that the Likud party, led by Netanyahu, had prepared and readied a file before the elections to invent this falsehood when the results were issued, because they know with absolute certainty that they will lose the elections.”

The intimidation campaign against Palestinian citizens of Israel materialised through aggressive police actions on election day. As reported by The Jerusalem Post, police arrested several Ra’am supporters for alleged vote-buying, which Likud immediately invoked to claim an attempt to steal the election. However, many of the suspects were quickly released, with a judge noting that suspicions had weakened and that investigators had failed to explain why restrictions were necessary. Defence lawyers maintained the seized funds were intended for charitable assistance.

“The best proof of this is that the detainees were released,” Tibi said. “We said from the beginning that the mountain laboured and brought forth a mouse.”

The security crackdown extended beyond party activists to media personnel. Abd Abu Shahadeh, a journalist and political activist, was arrested on Tuesday night by the Israeli police and the domestic security service, the Shin Bet.

Sami Abu Shehadeh, the chairman of the Balad Party, another member of the Joint List, called it an attempt by Netanyahu to “steal the elections”.

Human rights and Israeli affairs expert Mustafa Ibrahim argued that Netanyahu’s approach is deeply rooted in discriminatory state policy.

Ibrahim pointed to the treatment of Palestinians in Israel since the formation of the state in 1948 – when hundreds of thousands of Palestinians were forced out of their homes in the Nakba – including the period of military rule that was imposed on them until 1966.

Palestinian citizens of Israel have always been viewed as a “fifth column”, Ibrahim said, “and they are described as enemies of the state.”

Tibi emphasised that the suppression of Palestinian rights in Israel was part of a broader ongoing pattern.

“Political intimidation began on October 7 itself, when celebrities from our community were summoned for investigation simply for liking a post or writing a Quranic verse whose interpretation was distorted,” Tibi told Al Jazeera, referring to the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack on Israel.

He added that the decision in late September by the Israeli electoral committee to disqualify the Palestinian-led parties from the elections – later overturned by the Israeli Supreme Court – was part of that campaign.

“The tools multiplied and the goal is one, which is indeed to intimidate us from political work as candidates and voters,” Tibi said.

The political pressure from Netanyahu and his allies has engulfed Israeli state institutions. According to The Jerusalem Post, Shin Bet Director David Zini requested to interrogate senior Palestinian lawmakers, including Tibi and United Arab List leader Mansour Abbas, over foreign interference claims. Attorney-General Gali Baharav-Miara explicitly denied the request, leading to attacks from Netanyahu’s Likud party.

Abbas dismissed the allegations, calling the investigation reports as attempts to “smear the Arab public” and were unacceptable.

“I and all members of the United Arab List are not afraid of any investigation and are prepared to appear before any law enforcement authority,” Abbas said, provided the process is conducted under the attorney general and judicial system.

Far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir has demanded Baharav-Miara’s removal.

“Slowly but surely, they came to understand that this is a legal advisor who tried to incriminate a minister, tried to incriminate me, and ordered the Shin Bet chief to follow me and act against me. Just for that alone, she should have been sent home,” Ben-Gvir wrote on social media.

Abu Amer said that this was an example of Netanyahu avoiding direct confrontation and instead utilising figures like Ben-Gvir to carry out these tasks. “The attack on the Attorney-General is part of a systematic campaign, not a spontaneous one,” Abu Amer noted.

Ibrahim highlighted that this political incitement occurs against a backdrop of systemic racism.

“The targeting of the national minority with intimidation campaigns has been supported by the head of the government and the head of the state during the past few years,” Ibrahim said, adding that this came in the context of the killing of more than 190 people in Palestinian communities in Israel and in occupied East Jerusalem this year in violence that continues to ravage the community, and is partly blamed on a lack of policing and government funding.

The Palestinian-led parties are now focused on using their increased number of seats in parliament to address that issue, and others facing their community, while facing off against Netanyahu and his allies.

“In the past, they were annoyed by our patriotism only; today, they fear our influence. We hope it will actually backfire,” Tibi said. “The direct practical step is to overthrow them politically, and this comes through several procedures, operations, and a parliamentary step. But we will not stop at overthrowing them, rather we will work to improve the reality for the better.”

articles.title: Presidential hopeful Vance appears to question Iran war after polls debacle
articles.summary: US VP Vance cites trusted pollster saying Iran war, Israel ties were top of mind for Trump voters swinging to Democrats.
articles.body:
US Vice President JD Vance has blamed the war on Iran for his party’s withering midterms defeat, suggesting that the conflict may not have been worth ceding control of the United States Congress to Democrats.

“The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night,” Vance wrote in a lengthy post on X. “If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so.”

“Everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.”

Mark Pfeifle, who served as deputy national security adviser under President George W Bush, told Al Jazeera that Vance was owning up to a political failure of the administration’s own making.

“If you mess up, fess up!” he said, saying Vance was speaking up to convey that “my name was on the ballot two years ago. I have to take responsibility for this”, in a sign of political maturity and readiness to tackle Republicans’ biggest political liabilities.

Vance, a likely 2028 presidential candidate and heir apparent to US President Donald Trump’s Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement, has been a key negotiator as the US and Iran search for a way out of the eight-month conflict, which has dented their economies and pushed global fuel prices up.

His statements on Tehran have been more dovish than those of other key members of the administration, and his post-election note appears to mark the closest he has yet come to publicly diverging from Trump on an issue that looks set to dog Republicans as the war continues.

“Vance is definitely trying to distance himself from Trump, as many other respectable Republicans will do over the next several weeks and months,” said Nick Rahall, a former Democratic member of Congress. “The people have spoken.”

“It had even leaked before that JD was the only one in Trump’s inner circle who had questions and was hesitant about Iran [war] from the beginning,” Rahall added.

Citing a pollster he describes as “one of the smartest people I know”, Vance said he was told ending the Iran war and “changing our relationship with Israel” were two of the top four answers given by Americans surveyed who had voted for Trump in 2024 but were planning to vote for Democrats in the 2026 midterms.

In stark contrast, Trump said, in the wake of the rebuke at the ballot box , that he had no regrets about launching the conflict.

“I did the right thing. I would have done it again ,” he told the Wall Street Journal.

articles.title: Death toll hits 40 after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site, dozens remain missing
articles.summary: The death toll from a Russian bombing of an aid distribution point in Ukraine’s southeastern Zaporizhzhia region has risen to 40, ⁠with dozens still missing.
articles.body: The death toll from a Russian bombing of an aid distribution point in Ukraine’s southeastern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday has risen to 40, ⁠with dozens still missing, officials said, in one of the deadliest strikes on civilians this year. The attack came a day after a brief U.S.-brokered local ceasefire expired and less than a week before the United States is due to bring together Ukrainian and Russian delegations in Abu Dhabi for talks on ending the war, now in its fifth year. Reuters footage on Wednesday showed men in military fatigues loading bodies in white plastic bags into the back of a ⁠van in the village of Komyshuvakha, which was struck multiple times. Excavators were ​digging ⁠up earth near a huge blast crater while rescue workers searched underground for bodies. Ivan Fedorov, the co-head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Defense Council, wrote on Telegram that 59 people were missing. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said Russian forces first dropped aerial ⁠bombs on an underground school building being used as a distribution point as people arrived to collect aid, then struck the ​shelter with ⁠more bombs. Classes have long since been suspended at the ‌school because of its proximity to the front — Komyshuvakha lies some 11 miles from the nearest Russian positions — but it served as a shelter and handed out humanitarian aid every Monday, Zelenskyy said. Two members of a rescue crew and four police officers were among the ‌dead, emergency services said. Russia’s defense ministry said the attack targeted Ukrainian military units around ‌Komyshuvakha and two other settlements, and that up to 25 Ukrainian servicemen were killed. Russia and Ukraine both deny deliberately targeting civilians. Dramatic footage Bodycam footage from one of the policemen killed in the attack, which Ukrainian police posted and Reuters verified, shows rubble and badly damaged buildings in the aftermath of the initial aerial attacks. The policeman said the area was ⁠under threat from drones and appears to take shelter briefly inside the shell of a bombed-out building. Later in the footage, 15 to 20 people in civilian clothing are gathered outside the entrance to an underground shelter when a warning comes over a radio that Russian glide bombs are heading in the direction of the village. Residents rush down several flights of stairs and towards a room, while the policeman with the bodycam turns through a door into what appears to be a temporary police station. Three other men and a woman are visible in the final frames before there is a large explosion and the camera turns black. In a social media post accompanying the footage, the national police ‌said several strikes hit the area, including from a 3-ton FAB bomb, which is a large bomb fitted with ​a glide kit that allows it to fly long distances after being dropped from a Russian warplane. According to defense intelligence ‌websites, a 3-ton glide bomb would carry around 1.4 tons of ⁠explosives. Fighting resumes after brief local ceasefire The strike occurred a day after a six-day ceasefire to evacuate civilians from the ⁠Russian-occupied southern Ukrainian town of Oleshky expired. The truce, brokered by first lady Melania Trump, allowed nearly 800 people to be evacuated, according to the first lady. Zelenskyy awarded Trump a state honour for her ​role. The United States will bring together delegations from Ukraine and Russia in ‌Abu Dhabi on November 10 to 11 to discuss ending ​the conflict, postwar security agreements and de-escalation, US envoy Steve Witkoff said on Monday.

images.caption: Law enforcement officers and military personnel load the bodies of people killed in a Russian air strike into a van, in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, Ukraine, on Nov. 3, 2026.

articles.title: Netanyahu bet on Trump – but both lost
articles.summary: Israel’s political establishment grapples with US voter rejection of White House ally and own contribution towards it.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump and his Republican party’s resounding midterm defeat has left many in Israel, particularly on the political right, grappling with the scale of the rebuke to those seen as their closest allies in Washington.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has repeatedly sought to portray himself as almost uniquely qualified to maintain the unflinching support of Trump, who returned to the White House last year promising, among others, to not start “stupid foreign wars that never end”.

Yet in late February, Trump joined Netanyahu in ordering a joint military campaign against Iran, prompting immediate Iranian retaliation and raising the spectre of an all-out regional war. With the prospect of renewed hostilities looming, both leaders exchanged effusive endorsements in the build-up to Tuesday’s US congressional election and Israel’s parliamentary vote last week, calling upon the other’s electorate to head to the polls to support their ally.

The moves, however, seem to have either backfired or missed the mark dramatically.

Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition finished the October 27 electoral race with just 53 seats, far shy of the 61 needed to form a government. Trump’s party, meanwhile, lost control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate to Democratic challengers who made sweeping inroads into traditionally Republican territory, including the strongholds of Texas and Kansas.

“Obviously, what we have witnessed is a historic political tsunami that amounts to a total repudiation of Trumpism, so it’s certainly broader than one issue,” Shibley Telhami, of the University of Maryland and director of the Critical Issues Poll, said of the US midterm results. “But foreign policy was central, especially the Iran war and US backing of Israel, as Americans tie these to pocketbook issues,” he added.

The US is Israel’s staunchest diplomatic and military backer. Over the years, it has repeatedly used its United Nations Security Council veto to block dozens of resolutions critical of Israel, including several motions calling for an end to the genocidal war against the Palestinians in the Gaza Strip.

At the same time, it has been providing Israel with at least $3.8bn in military aid annually, allowing it to acquire the cutting-edge US weaponry that has granted it military superiority across the region – assistance, however, that is carrying an increasingly high political cost.

Polling overseen by Telhami a week ago found that a majority of people in the US believed that Israel had influenced the Trump administration’s decision to instigate the costly and protracted war with Iran. The survey indicated that Washington’s close relationship with Tel Aviv had become more of a liability than an asset for many in the electorate, Telhami noted, “with most saying specifically Israel would be a factor in their vote. An even larger majority said the Iran war, which they tie to Israel, would impact their vote”.

While Trump acknowledged the Democrats’ midterm win, and reluctantly conceded that the war on Iran was partly to blame due to its impact on energy prices, Netanyahu has spent the days since his own electoral defeat questioning the results.

Over the past week, the Likud party leader has falsely accused foreign powers of illegally boosting the vote for Israel’s Arab-led parties and cited his victory among Jewish voters as the basis for a national government. In his most recent echo of Trump’s reaction to his own loss in the 2020 US presidential election, Netanyahu even threatened not to recognise the certification of the results.

But as Israel enters a period of coalition wrangling, its political establishment also has to grapple with the routing of its White House ally and its potential culpability in it.

On Wednesday, key opposition figure Yair Lapid said almost all of Netanyahu’s actions since the vote, including his call for the internal security service Shin Bet to investigate the leaders of the Arab parties, in conjunction with the US election results, had rendered the prime minister politically noxious.

With voting still ongoing on Tuesday, Trump said in a TV interview he had made a deal with Netanyahu that ⁠⁠the US would no longer be providing funding of “$4bn a year” to Israel after the end of 2026. While details remain scarce, the timing prompted speculation that Trump’s comments were part of a bid to stave off public anger over his administration’s support for Israel and a time of mounting domestic economic pressure.

“There’s a degree of denial inside Israel as to the depth of the change that is taking place in the US,” former Israeli government adviser Daniel Levy told Al Jazeera, caveating that while Israel itself may not have been on the midterm ballot, the sense of the “tail wagging the dog” in how Netanyahu’s relationship with Trump was perceived, certainly was.

“Most palpable was, of course, the effect of the Iran war,” said Levy. “Part of that is the Israeli role in dragging a gullible president into another calamitous Middle East military adventure.”

The war also brought a sense of clarity to the US public over their country’s relationship with Israel and the electoral cost of launching further wars in the Middle East, he added.

That the US’s full-throated support for Israel may be shifting in the face of growing international isolation might as well be on the minds of Israel’s opposition leaders as they weigh their coalition options. Netanyahu may be reviled by some within the US Democratic Party, but his relationship with Trump could still give him the political space to foment a new push for escalating the war against Iran, the political consequences of which could even see him once more able to set the agenda, Levy suggested.

“Netanyahu’s hand will now be weaker in trying to achieve that, but it should not be dismissed altogether – certainly not with a wounded Trump at the helm,” he said.

For Alon Pinkas, a former Israeli ambassador and consul general in New York, the relationship between the US and Israel had reached “a real inflection point, the consequences of which I don’t think much of Israel has either the imagination or education to truly understand”.

Much will depend on the Iran war and Trump’s reaction to the dramatic rejection of him and his policy agenda at the polls, Pinkas said, which could see him either escalate the conflict or seek an agreement that might appease Congress.

Either way, the future ties between the US and Israel had fundamentally changed, he argued.

“Even with all the speculation that the ending of the $3.8bn grant was some kind of quid pro quo to satisfy the US public, there was still no mention of the access to the weaponry that’s part of that grant,” said Pinkas.

“The money, Israel could probably live without; the weaponry, it depends upon – but there was no mention of that,” he added. “There was no mention of any future strategic agreement. It’s all just in the air.”

articles.title: Ukraine says bodycam video shows deadly Russian double-tap bombing
articles.summary: At least 40 people were killed and another 30 may still be under the rubble after Monday's attack on a Ukrainian village, Kyiv says.
articles.body:
A bodycam video has been released by Ukraine police which they say shows the moments between two powerful Russian bomb strikes that killed at least 40 people at an aid centre and a shelter.

The footage, from a camera on one of the killed police officers, shows residents of the southern village of Kamyshuvakha going to an underground shelter after the first attack on Monday. Soon after a blast is heard and flames are seen as the shelter is hit.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said more than 30 people may still be under the rubble, as a search operation continued for the third day.

Nine gliding bombs, some weighing 3,000kg, hit the village as people had gathered to get humanitarian aid, Ukraine said.

The bodycam footage was released by Ukraine's national police on Wednesday.

It shows huge devastation after the first bomb strike on the village in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, as shocked local residents stare at the rubble.

Severely damaged buildings are also seen.

A voice of a military official is then heard on a two-way radio warning police on the ground of more glide bombs being launched towards Kamyshuvakha.

"Quickly [go] to the shelter!" one of the police officers tells local residents, who are seen walking into the shelter - at least two floors underground.

Seconds later the shelter is hit, and the recording stops.

Ukraine said the shelter was near a local school, which was being used to distribute humanitarian aid.

BBC Verify has confirmed the video was filmed in the same place as footage released by the Ukrainian state emergencies service DSNS showing the aftermath Monday's attack in Komyshuvakha.

In a post on social media on Wednesday, Zelensky said that "nine aerial bombs were dropped by the Russians.

"First, they hit people who came to receive humanitarian aid, and then rescuers and police officers who arrived at the scene."

The Ukrainian president added that "unfortunately, there has been very little reaction from the world to this insane attack", describing it as yet another of "thousands" of war crimes committed by Russia.

Ukraine's DSNS earlier posted another video showing a huge crater left after the attack on Kamyshuvakha.

The Russian military has not publicly commented.

Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

In a separate development on Wednesday, Zelensky said he talked "in great detail for an hour-and-a-half" with US President Donald Trump's peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner ahead of trilateral negotiations between Ukraine, Russia and the US on 10-11 November in Abu-Dhabi.

The Ukrainian leader - who is currently making a surprise visit to Spain - also said his team had a separate "meaningful" meeting in Brussels with representatives from the US, the EU, France, Britain, Germany, as well as Nato and the World Bank about "post-war reconstruction".

He added that the meeting in Belgium's capital would continue on Thursday to discuss "security guarantees" for Ukraine.

Since the trilateral talks aimed at ending the war were suspended in February, Moscow has stepped up attacks as Kyiv virtually ran out of Western-supplied interceptors to defend against missiles.

Analysts expect no major breakthrough when the talks resume in the capital of the United Arab Emirates.
