articles.title: Iran’s Hormuz exemption likely to bring relief to India’s oil importers
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Iran has exempted commercial ships from four countries, including India and China, from transit restrictions in Strait of Hormuz, a senior
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Iran has exempted commercial ships from four countries, including India and China, from transit restrictions in Strait of Hormuz, a senior Iranian lawmaker has said, amid continued attacks on vessels attempting to cross the strategic energy corridor. The statement has raised hopes among shipping lines of resuming voyages to transport crude oil, gas and fertilisers after a gap of nearly eight months.Shipping industry executives, however, said they were in “wait and watch” mode and would seek greater clarity before deciding to send vessels through the strait. They said the reported exemption could significantly reduce security risks for Indian ships and seafarers.In an interview with Iranian Students’ News Agency (ISNA) Tuesday, Amir Hayat-Moghaddam, deputy chairman of Iranian Parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, said, “We have currently exempted four countries — India, China, Iraq and Qatar — from transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz. Ships from these countries pass freely, and the Americans do not intercept them either.”Moghaddam said the exemptions were based on specific considerations and mutual interests. Facilitating the passage of Indian ships was intended to enable imports of medicines from India, while the exemption for Chinese vessels was aimed at securing Beijing’s political support.The Strait of Hormuz, which connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman, handles around 20% of global energy supplies in normal times. India imports nearly 90% of its crude oil requirements, with about 30% of its imports passing through the strait.“We have not sent any ships since April. If our vessels and crew face no security risks, we can resume sending ships. This would provide huge relief, as insurance premiums could fall sharply and logistics costs would come down because of shorter voyage times through the strait,” said a senior shipping line executive.Oil refiners said a resumption of normal vessel movement through Strait of Hormuz would improve crude availability and help ease prices, which have remained around $110 a barrel or higher over the past two months.Nikhil Dubey, lead analyst at Kpler, said higher freight costs for Russian crude had eroded its delivered-price advantage, while improving supplies from West Asia were offering refiners more competitive alternatives.Crude imports from West Asia rose to around 2.7 million barrels per day in Sept, the highest since Feb, accounting for about 54% of India’s total imports. articles.title: Cumberland Council commits to talks about Carlisle flights return
articles.summary: A motion pledges to start talks about supporting commercial routes at Carlisle Airport.
articles.body:
A council has committed to start talks aimed at returning commercial flights to its region.

Carlisle airport, in Cumbria, started running commercial routes in 2019 after a 25-year hiatus, but stopped operating them in 2020 due to the coronavirus pandemic and they never resumed.

In a motion approved at a meeting on Tuesday, Cumberland Council committed to engaging with the airport owners, the government and other local authorities to support a return of commercial flights to the region.

Leader of the Labour-led authority Mark Fryer said proposals could form part of a transport plan when Cumbria's mayoral authority comes into being next year.

"Let's be under no illusion that to do it is going to be really, really tough, but that doesn't mean we shouldn't work hard to make it a success," Fryer said.

The nearest airports to Carlisle are in Newcastle, Glasgow, Edinburgh and Manchester - Fryer said they attracted high numbers of passengers and already had good infrastructure.

He said a mayoral authority would be best placed to liaise with the government to seek funding to support potential operations in Carlisle.

"It'd be difficult for a small local authority to plough millions of pounds into a project like that."

Independent councillor Robert Betton, who brought the motion to the table, said it did not ask the council "to promise flights or commit to major spending".

"It asks us to work with the airport's owners and other partners to explore what is possible."

Under Stobart Group's ownership in 2019, Scottish-based company Loganair ran flights from Carlisle to Dublin, Belfast and London Southend.

Cumbria Tourism said those routes had made Cumbria "easier to access" and provided links to international markets, such as for passengers travelling from the US via Ireland.

Managing director Gill Haigh said the organisation had been supportive of the flights and were disappointed when they ended.

"There is clearly a lot that would need to be worked through before any passenger services could return."

AW Jenkinson took over responsibility for the Carlisle Lake District Airport in 2024 and has since increased use for military training for UK and NATO forces, acted as a base for search and rescue helicopters and opened a cafe there.

A spokesperson for the firm said commercial routes would require investment "potentially running into millions of pounds", with sufficient passenger demand to make them viable.

"Obsolete" systems at the airport also meant limited appeal from potential operators.

"Aircraft currently rely on visual approaches, meaning poor weather or reduced visibility can prevent them from landing," the spokesperson said.

Aviation expert John Strickland, who has 44 years of experience in the industry, said it was a tough market for regional airports.

"It'd be an enormous challenge to achieve a successful commercial proposition [in Carlisle]."

He said he would not be surprised to see airlines fail throughout Europe this winter due to high fuel costs and any investment needed to make commercial flights work at Carlisle airport would be "disproportionate" to the chances of attracting a sustainable operation.

"Many small airports in many countries have actually closed and if they run they tend to run at a loss."

AW Jenkinson said it was currently operating as an "unlicensed aerodrome", but work was under way to open up to more users.

A spokesperson said it aimed to allow small-scale private charters by 2027 and update its systems the following year, hoping to make it "more attractive" to potential operators.

The spokesperson said: "While we are also actively exploring other opportunities to make the best use of the airport's facilities, we would also welcome the opportunity to be involved in any future discussions Cumberland Council may have, regarding the future and feasibility of the airport going forward."

articles.title: In 1910, Harry Houdini's wife gave him a pocket watch engraved with a secret message spelling his birth name; 116 years later, it sold for $204,000 at auction, more than five times its $40,000 high estimate
articles.summary: Harry Houdini was famous for escaping locked boxes, handcuffs and seemingly impossible restraints, but one of the most personal objects connected to him
articles.body: Harry Houdini was famous for escaping locked boxes, handcuffs and seemingly impossible restraints, but one of the most personal objects connected to him carried a secret hidden in plain sight. In 1910, his wife Beatrice, known as Bess, gave him a gold-filled pocket watch engraved with what appeared to be a simple birthday message. More than a century later, Potter & Potter Auctions sold the watch for $204,000, far above its $20,000 to $40,000 estimate, as per their website. The reason for the extraordinary price is the inscription inside the case. At first glance, it reads like an affectionate note from Bess to her husband. But the first letters of the central words spell “EHRICH,” the birth name Houdini was born with as Erik Weisz. That small act of concealment, combined with the watch’s direct link to Houdini and Bess, helped turn a 19th-century timepiece into one of the most sought-after Houdini artefacts ever offered at auction. Read more about it here, as per details on the auction house's website:A gift with a hidden nameThe watch was presented to Houdini by Bess on his 36th birthday in 1910. Engraved inside the hunting case are the words: “For Harry / Ever Houdini / Remembering In / Complete Happiness / BESS / 3/24/10.” The message looks like a romantic dedication, but the capitalised first letters of the middle words form a private code: E, H, R, I, C and H.Together, those letters spell “Ehrich,” the name Houdini used before he became the world-famous escape artist. The engraving gives the watch a double identity. Publicly, it is a birthday gift from a wife to her husband. Privately, it preserves the name he carried before fame transformed him into “Houdini.”Potter & Potter described the object as a 19th-century French gold-filled cylinder pocket watch with an attractively engraved hunting case. It measures roughly 1 11/16 inches across and comes with its winding key. The auction house noted that the mechanism is in working condition but needs servicing, while the watch remains in near-fine condition with only tiny signs of handling.A birthday in AustraliaThe gift carries historical weight beyond its inscription. Bess gave Houdini the watch while the couple were touring Australia, just six days after he made a historic flight at Diggers Rest. That flight made Houdini the first person to pilot an aeroplane in Australia, adding a major achievement to a career already built on daring public performances.The date engraved in the watch, March 24, 1910, is also significant. Houdini often gave April 6 as his birthday and signed autographs with that date, telling his brother Hardeen that it was the birthday recognised by his mother. According to the auction listing, however, his true birthday was March 24, the date Bess chose to engrave inside the case.That detail makes the watch more than a collectible. It is a private record of Houdini’s real birth date, preserved by the person who knew him most intimately. For collectors, that combination of romance, secrecy and biographical importance is exceptionally rare.Why collectors paid so muchHoudini memorabilia attracts strong interest because his life combined showmanship, mystery and personal reinvention. He was born Erik Weisz in Budapest in 1874, later changed his name to Harry Houdini, and built a global reputation as an escape artist, magician, aviator, author and investigator of spiritualist claims. An object connected directly to both his public persona and his private identity naturally commands attention.The watch also has an unusually clear provenance. After Houdini’s death in 1926, it was owned by the noted mentalist and magician Joseph Dunninger. It later passed to collector Raphael Ellenbogen and then to Kevin Connolly. Ellenbogen’s account of the watch and its acquisition was published in Magicol in May 1988, giving collectors a documented history of the object.That chain of ownership matters in the auction market. A Houdini-linked artefact is valuable, but one that can be traced through respected magicians and collectors is far more credible. The watch’s story, condition and inscription together made it a centrepiece of Potter & Potter’s “Houdini Returns: The Centennial Auction,” held on October 31, 2026.The auction resultThe watch was listed as Lot 20 with an estimate of $20,000 to $40,000. It attracted 13 bids before selling for $204,000, a price that includes the buyer’s premium. That result is more than five times the high estimate and demonstrates how competitive the market for authenticated Houdini material has become.Auction results like this reflect more than scarcity. The watch is small, personal and tied to a specific moment in Houdini’s life. It was not a stage prop used in a famous escape, but a private gift from Bess that carried a hidden reference to the name he left behind.For collectors, that intimacy is often what turns an object into a trophy. The watch can be held in one hand, yet it connects directly to Houdini’s marriage, his birth identity, his Australian tour and one of the most important years of his performing career.A message that outlived the magicianHoudini died in 1926, but the watch has preserved a private message for 116 years. Its inscription does not announce itself as a code. It requires a closer look, which is fitting for an object connected to a man whose career depended on hiding the truth in plain sight.The final price shows that collectors value not only famous names but also the stories behind objects. In this case, the story belongs to Bess as much as Houdini. She gave her husband a watch, marked the date she believed was his real birthday and quietly encoded the name he was born with.A century later, that hidden message helped the pocket watch escape its estimate. It sold for $204,000, becoming a lasting reminder that even the world’s greatest escape artist could not escape the people and memories that shaped him.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Deco's singer says number one album was 'worth the hard work'
articles.summary: Synth-pop band Deco are celebrating after the chart success of their second album Dreamhouse.
articles.body:
The lead singer of synth-pop band Deco says the success of their latest album has made "all those hard times worth it".

Dreamhouse, the Staffordshire group's second record, was released in October and reached number one on the official independent album breakers chart.

It was also in the top 11 of the independent, record store, homegrown, downloads, cassettes, CDs, sales and physical albums charts.

Max Kendall, lead singer, said it meant a lot to the band and "eclipsed" the moments they wished they were "doing something else", but it had yet to sink in.

"It's very hard work, but it makes all those hard times worth it," he told BBC Radio Stoke.

"We were not expecting to get in the charts," he added. "We were just happy to get the second album out there.

"We were proud of the actual music on it as well, more than ever before. It was something that we ourselves would listen to."

While he did not want to describe his job as "insanely difficult", Kendall said he felt like he had "not really stopped" since committing himself to the music since he was a teenager.

"I've just grabbed it by the horns, I suppose," he added.

The band formed in 2011 and consists of Kendall, his sister Lucy Kendall, Jonathan Dell and Thomas Reinholz.

They have tens of millions of views across social media and have performed live alongside the likes of Nile Rodgers, A-ha, McFly and The Human League.

The success of Dreamhouse, described as a colourful escape from the chaos of 2026, came after a tiring chart campaign, with the band doing much of the promotion themselves.

"I've always had these little targets and almost forced them to happen," Kendall said. "With the chart campaign, I was up late every single day campaigning.

"It takes a lot to make things happen, maybe more so than a lot of bands because we're doing a lot of these things ourselves. It feels even sweeter when it happens when you don't expect it."

Kendall said they were now focused on their current tour, with upcoming headline shows at Rock City in Nottingham on Saturday and Manchester Academy on 20 November.

They were then hoping to take a break from recording albums, with potential plans to release some EPs before getting into the next album cycle.

"It's exhausting; we've done two [albums] in two years, and it's a lot," Kendall said. "I've not had a holiday for four years, so I'm looking forward to that."

articles.title: The best makeup remover for every type of makeup
articles.summary: Dermatologists explain how to choose the best makeup remover for waterproof, long-wear and everyday makeup, plus the products they recommend.
articles.body: Removing makeup at the end of a long day or night out is one of my least favorite parts of my routine, and I’ll admit that it’s a step I sometimes skip. To make matters worse, when I do remove it, I’ll sometimes see leftover foundation on my towel after washing my face, or mascara residue under my eyes the next morning. So, does the remover you use depend on the type of makeup you’re wearing? I spoke to dermatologists and skin care experts about the best makeup removers to use based on the makeup you wear, and how to make sure your skin is completely clean before bed. I also rounded up expert-recommended makeup removers and NBC Selected editor favorites. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter Does the type of makeup you wear determine what type of makeup remover to use? Yes, and it’s actually one of the most overlooked parts of a typical skin care routine. “Makeup formulas behave in very different ways, so a remover that works well on a light skin tint may do very little against waterproof mascara,” says Dr. Gina Maccarone, triple board-certified cosmetic surgeon and founder of The Surgeonista. “When you match the remover to the formula, you remove makeup completely with less rubbing, and that protects the skin barrier over time.” What type of makeup remover is best? Turns out, there’s no one-size-fits-all makeup remover, and the type of makeup you’re wearing usually determines how you remove it. Below, I list a few popular types of makeup and the best products to remove each one based on my experts’ guidance. Waterproof mascara and eyeliner: Waterproof makeup is hydrophobic, meaning it repels water, so water-based cleansers alone may not effectively remove it. Instead, use an oil-based or bi-phase remover to break down those water-repelling agents. “Bi-phase eye makeup remover is typically best, as it has both an oil phase and a water phase,” says Katharine Perry, board-certified nurse practitioner at MONA Dermatology. “The oil phase helps to break down the product, and the water phase helps to flush any residue.” Long-wear or matte lipstick: An oil or cleansing balm loosens long-wear lipstick much better than micellar water or a foaming cleanser, says Maccarone.Full-coverage foundation and concealer: Use a cleansing oil or balm as a first step. “These formulas often contain silicones and pigments that oil dissolves well, and massaging an oil over dry skin lifts the makeup without aggressive rubbing,” says Maccarone. Follow it up with a gentle water-based cleanser to clean your skin afterward.Tinted moisturizers and skin tints: “Lighter makeup can still have some of those staying power ingredients, so it’s best to know what is actually in your makeup when deciding on a cleanser,” says Perry. Lightweight makeup usually comes off with a gentle cleanser, but those with sunscreen might be harder to remove. “If you’re wearing sunscreen under your skin tint, which I always recommend, a quick pass with micellar water or a cleansing oil first helps make sure everything is fully removed,” says Maccarone. Liquid and cream makeup: Foundations, blushes, contours and other makeup with a cream or liquid formula, especially long-wear ones, bind more closely to the skin and usually benefit from an oil or balm first, says Maccarone. “The more a product is designed to last, the more thoughtful the removal step needs to be,” she says.Powder foundation, blush and bronzer: “Powder doesn’t have the same adherence to the skin as a liquid product would, so a gentle cleanser usually works,” says Perry. Best makeup removers overall Maccarone recommends this cleansing balm for full-coverage or long-wear makeup, but it’s a great option for any type of makeup you use. “It melts on contact, dissolves foundation and sunscreen without harsh rubbing and rinses clean,” she says. It’s also one of our favorite cleansers for acne-prone skin because it’s gentle and won’t clog pores. “It melts makeup away so easily that even trickier products, like tubing and waterproof mascara, are easy to take off,” says NBC Selected associate SEO reporter Ashley Morris. “Another upside is that I don’t have to do much rubbing; after I swipe it across my face, I can go right in to rinse it off without having to knead or pull at my skin.” As someone with sensitive skin, I’ve used dozens of makeup removers that have caused redness and irritation. This Farmacy cleansing balm is one that actually worked at removing makeup, even tough mascara and liquid eyeliner, without stripping my skin or creating red, blotchy spots on my face. It does have a subtle scent, but it doesn’t leave that dry, tight feeling that’s so common after cleansing. Maccarone and Perry both recommend Bioderma’s oil-free micellar water for sensitive skin or lighter makeup days because it’s gentle, fragrance-free and well-tolerated by most skin types, she says. It’s also a favorite of NBC Selected editorial operations associate Jem Alabi, who came across this micellar water while studying abroad in Paris for a semester and was “thrilled” to find it on Amazon when she came back. “As a waterproof mascara lover, this product doesn’t sting, leave my skin too dry and red, or have an astringent smell,” she says. Best for waterproof mascara and eye makeup This expert-recommended micellar water is extremely versatile: It removes eye makeup, dirt and sunscreen without causing irritation or stinging. To remove waterproof mascara and eyeliner, apply the micellar water on a cotton pad and hold it gently against your closed eyes for about 15 to 30 seconds, which loosens up the makeup and makes it come off easier, says Ostad. Plus, you don’t need to rinse it off afterward Using a cleansing oil is one of the most effective ways to remove stubborn, heavy and waterproof makeup since it breaks down the product quicker, experts say. It comes recommended by Maccarone, who says it emulsifies beautifully with water, which makes it a good option even for people who worry about oil cleansers. It also has vitamin E to moisturize skin and it won’t clog pores, according to the brand. Best for full-coverage foundation and concealer This cleanser, which starts off as a balm and turns into an oil as you massage it into your skin, comes recommended by both Perry and board-certified dermatologist Dr. Annette Czernik. “It does a great job of breaking down makeup, even heavier foundation and waterproof products,” says Czernik. It has a blend of antioxidants and oils that give your skin extra moisture, so it leaves your skin feeling soft instead of dry or tight. “It’s a little more expensive than some other makeup removers, but I think it’s a good option for someone who wears makeup regularly,” says Czernik. The balm does have a subtle scent, but luckily it doesn’t linger once you wash it off, experts say. “For the longest time, makeup wipes were my go-to for taking off my makeup, no matter how much I was wearing. That was until I discovered cleansing balms, and this one from Reale Actives melts off my makeup in just a few minutes while simultaneously hydrating and cleansing my skin,” says NBC Selected associate social media editor Caitlin Cusack. Even when she has a full face of makeup on, this cleansing balm does a great job of breaking down makeup without irritating her sensitive, acne-prone skin. Plus, it doesn’t burn or sting her sensitive eyes even when wearing her most stubborn mascaras, she says. “I still wash my face with a water-based cleanser after using the cleansing balm, so it adds an extra step to my routine, but I’m willing to spend the extra time if it means preventing makeup buildup and acne,” says Cusack. I love this cleansing balm: It turns from a solid to a milky consistency that moisturizes and smooths my skin while seamlessly breaking down my makeup. Plus, a little goes a very long way, so the tub lasts me for months after using it one to three times a week. It has elderberry oil, which is high in essential fatty acids that help regulate oil production and hydrate skin; starflower oil, which reduces water loss and inflammation; and padina pavonica, a type of Mediterranean brown algae known for hydrating, according to the brand. Best for matte and long-wear lipstick I’ve used this cleansing oil for over a year, and it’s one I instantly reach for if I’m wearing a darker matte lipstick or dark-colored eyeshadow. A few minutes of gently rubbing this cleansing oil into my lips and eyes takes off the color almost immediately. Since my lips are one of the most sensitive parts of my face and get dry and red easily, I love that this cleansing oil is gentle and fragrance-free to avoid any irritation. It also leaves absolutely no residue, doesn’t leave a gross taste in my mouth when I use it, and is noncomedogenic, so it won’t clog your pores if you choose to use it on the rest of your face. Best for powder makeup Since powder doesn’t adhere to the skin as well as liquid or cream makeup products, you don’t need a super powerful makeup remover, experts say. If I’m wearing powder makeup, a little bit of concealer or a tinted moisturizer and need something quick and easy to remove it, or if I have some leftover mascara under my eyes in the morning, I reach for these gentle cleansing pads. They remove a light amount of makeup with just a few swipes, and I don’t have to rinse it off afterward (which comes in handy on lazy days). I’ve also been traveling a lot this year and they’re small enough to fit comfortably in my travel backpack, which means I always have a makeup remover on hand. Keep in mind they won’t remove heavy eye makeup or long-wear foundation, so you’ll need to use a cleansing balm or oil beforehand to get it all off. I take a travel-size version of this cleanser whenever I go on a trip because it leaves my skin clean and hydrated, and it removes my lighter makeup and powders, which means I don’t have to take both a makeup remover and a cleanser in my travel bag. I love how gentle it is on my sensitive, acne-prone skin, and the light, gel-like texture doesn’t leave my skin feeling stripped and tight. Does removing eye makeup require special consideration? Yes, you should be careful when removing your eye makeup. “You never want to aggressively rub your eyes because the skin around them is delicate, and too much pulling can irritate your eyes or damage your lashes,” says dermatologist and reconstructive surgeon Dr. Ariel Ostad. One trick is to soak a cotton pad with a remover and gently hold it against your closed eye for about 15 to 30 seconds, which gives the product time to loosen the makeup before you wipe it away, says Ostad. Glitter, shimmer or highly pigmented eye makeup can be especially tricky because those tiny particles can get into your eyes. “I’d recommend using a gentle cleansing balm that’s safe for the eye area, since it can help break down stubborn makeup without a lot of rubbing,” says Ostad. What is the difference between cleansing oils, cleansing balms and micellar water? These are the most popular types of makeup removers, and they can have different functions depending on the type of makeup you’re using. Cleansing oils dissolve oil-based and waterproof makeup. They usually have emulsifiers, so they turn milky and rinse away when you add water, says Maccarone. Cleansing oils are great for removing heavier makeup, especially long-wearing foundation and waterproof products.Cleansing balms do the same thing as a cleansing oil, but have a solid texture that melts when it makes contact with your skin, which many people find easier to control, says Maccarone. They’re good for stubborn makeup, including full-coverage foundation and eye makeup, says Ostad. Micellar water contains micelles, which are tiny clusters of mild cleansing molecules that attract and lift oil and makeup without needing to rinse, says Maccarone. You can usually use micellar water with a cotton pad to lift dirt, oil and makeup off your skin, says Perry. It’s usually a good choice for lighter makeup like tinted moisturizer, blush and regular mascara, and it’s convenient if you want to remove a little makeup without washing your entire face, says Ostad. However, if you’re using heavy or long-wear makeup, it might not be enough, so you should wash your face afterward. Are makeup remover wipes actually effective? Makeup wipes are good in a pinch and better than not washing at all, but they shouldn’t be your primary removal method. “One of the biggest issues is that they don’t always remove all the makeup, oil and dirt sitting on your skin,” says Czernik. “You also tend to rub your face more when using wipes, which can cause irritation, especially around your eyes. I’d treat them as a backup option and wash your face afterward whenever possible.” How to choose a makeup remover based on your skin type When choosing the right makeup remover for you, keep in mind what kind of makeup you’re using first, then narrow down your options based on your skin type. Here’s what works best for common skin types: Dry skin: Use a cleansing balm or oil to remove makeup, which won’t strip your skin of its moisture, says Czernik.Oily or acne-prone skin: Look for a lightweight remover that rinses off easily and won’t clog your pores, says Czernik. Oily and combination skin can still use cleansing oils, ideally lightweight ones that rinse cleanly, followed by a gentle cleanser, says Maccarone.Sensitive skin: Avoid products with common irritants like fragrance or alcohols, says Czernik. Consider using a fragrance-free micellar water since that’s less likely to cause redness and irritation. Keep in mind that for more sensitive skin types (like acne-, rosacea- and eczema-prone skin), heavier makeup and oil-based cleansers may be more irritating, so consider sticking with lightweight skin tints and gentle cleansers, says Perry. Meet our skin care experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Gina Maccarone is a triple board-certified cosmetic surgeon and founder of The SurgeonistaKatharine Perry is a board-certified nurse practitioner at MONA Dermatology.Dr. Ariel Ostad is a New York City-based dermatologist and reconstructive surgeon.Dr. Annette Czernik is a board-certified dermatologist and founder of DermMedical in Stamford, Connecticut. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected who has written about skin care, hair care and beauty for more than six years. I’ve also tested dozens of makeup removers over the past few years to determine the best ones to shop. articles.title: WHO approves trials for two new Ebola vaccines
articles.summary: Two new vaccines were designed for the Bundibugyo virus that has killed more than 5,300 in the DR Congo.
articles.body:
The World Health Organization (WHO) has approved clinical trials for two new Ebola vaccines, as doctors fight to control the largest outbreak in the history of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

On Monday, WHO expert groups recommended adding two vaccine trials designed to fight the Bundibugyo strain, which has killed more than 5,300 people, most in the DRC, since May.

Public health agencies have struggled to contain the Bundibugyo virus, which has a fatality rate of 50 percent due to the lack of a vaccine or treatments designed specifically for the strain.

WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said a trial that began last month used the Ervebo vaccine, which was approved for the Zaire strain of the Ebola virus but is not designed for Bundibugyo.

Tedros said the new vaccines undergoing trials are designed specifically for the Bundibugyo virus. Results from the vaccine trial are expected in early 2027, the WHO reported.

The DRC’s National Institute for Biomedical Research is leading the trial, backed by the WHO and other partners, said Tedros. The vaccine was developed by the University of Oxford with the Serum Institute of India and Moderna.

“Vaccines are powerful tools, but they are not substitutes for the proven measures that can save lives now: early care, contact tracing, isolation, safe and dignified burials and trusted engagement with communities,” he added.

The African Centres for Disease Control and Prevention said 10,444 cases of the Bundibugyo virus have been confirmed, making it the fastest-growing outbreak in DRC’s history.

In Kenya , nine cases have been reported, including two deaths. One case has been confirmed in Nigeria , according to the WHO.

Tedros urged that travel restrictions imposed by some countries be lifted, warning that they could discourage transparent reporting.

“Such restrictions punish countries for doing the right thing, create disincentives for transparency, and harm the response,” said Tedros.

The WHO said it is supporting all countries neighbouring DRC to prepare for cases to spread across borders.

Meanwhile, a British healthcare worker infected with Ebola is being ⁠evacuated from the DRC to the United Kingdom for specialist treatment, a UK government spokesperson said.

In a statement, the government said the patient is in a stable condition and is expected to arrive ⁠in the UK by Thursday, then be transferred to a high-consequence infectious disease unit.

The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains ‌low, the statement said.

articles.title: ‘Vast criminal network’: US sanctions Indian couple, linked firms over maritime fraud aiding Iran’s oil trade
articles.summary: The United States on Wednesday imposed sanctions on an India-based businessman, his wife and several Indian companies for allegedly helping Iran evade
articles.body: The United States on Wednesday imposed sanctions on an India-based businessman, his wife and several Indian companies for allegedly helping Iran evade international restrictions on its oil trade through a network involved in maritime fraud.The US Treasury Department identified Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, as the alleged operators of a "vast criminal network" that provided false flags and fraudulent maritime certifications to vessels transporting Iranian petroleum. The network allegedly helped sanctioned ships, including those operating on behalf of Iran's military and its proxies, continue their operations.The sanctions were announced under the Trump administration's "Operation Economic Outcast", which aims to cut off Iran's ability to generate revenue through oil exports and other economic activities.The US Treasury also named Indian nationals Ashwani Kumar Dhiman and Ishwinder Singh, who it said served as directors of businesses associated with Sharma's network, along with nine India-based entities linked to the network.In a post on X, the US Treasury said Sharma and Shahid had supported Iran's shadow fleet through a web of maritime fraud. It alleged that their operations provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum, including ships working for Iran's military and its proxies.How Indian network allegedly helped Iran evade sanctionsAccording to the US Treasury, Sharma and Shahid operated the network from Chandigarh and allegedly established fraudulent maritime registries by impersonating the authorities of several countries.AFP reported that the couple's operations involved creating websites that falsely claimed to provide ship registration, flagging, seafarer training and vessel classification services on behalf of different countries without their authorisation.The alleged operations date back to 2014, when the couple reportedly attempted to impersonate the maritime flagging authority of the Caribbean nation of Dominica.In 2023, Sharma established Singapore-based Eswatini Maritime Affairs and International Ship Registry PTE Ltd. Despite being publicly disowned by Eswatini authorities, the organisation allegedly continued providing registration services to vessels transporting Iranian oil.The Treasury also identified websites that falsely claimed to offer maritime registration services on behalf of countries and territories including Aruba, Guyana, Mali, Mozambique, Malawi, Sint Maarten and Timor-Leste.The US alleged that several sanctioned vessels used the fraudulent registries to transport Iranian oil despite international restrictions. Among the entities targeted were Oceaniek Technologies India, Aryavart Ship Management, Precept Trends, Polynesia Maritime, Alexarya Finserv, Alexarya Media and Entertainment, Viharaboating and Aryavart Maritime and Educational Trust.The Treasury said Oceaniek Technologies India was used to set up fraudulent ship registries, while Shahid took over the management of several businesses linked to the network as scrutiny of Sharma increased.US warns of action against Iran's supportersUS Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reiterated Washington's warning that individuals and organisations supporting Iran would face sanctions.In a post on X, Bessent said the administration would continue targeting those helping the Iranian regime, whether through land, sea or air. He also warned that those involved in supporting Tehran's activities could not expect to escape US action."As we have said many times, under Operation Economic Outcast, you are either with us or against us," Bessent said.The Treasury said fraudulent ship registrations allow vessels to evade international restrictions and maritime regulations.It also warned that falsely flagged ships may lack valid protection and indemnity insurance, potentially exposing countries to financial and environmental liabilities in the event of accidents in their territorial waters.In a separate action on Wednesday, Washington sanctioned Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services Inc for allegedly continuing to provide support to Iran's heavily sanctioned aviation sector.The latest move is part of a broader US campaign to restrict Iran's oil revenues and economic networks amid the ongoing conflict with Tehran.You use AI every day. articles.title: An Ohio father sued police over his son's fatal shooting after a highway crash, filing the case himself before the deadline; after hiring a lawyer, his suit was still dismissed, but a federal appeals court has revived it
articles.summary: A father's attempt to seek justice for his son suffered a legal setback even after he followed a court's instructions to hire an attorney.
articles.body: A father's attempt to seek justice for his son suffered a legal setback even after he followed a court's instructions to hire an attorney. The case involves the fatal shooting of Elijah Isham by police officers in Moraine, Ohio, following a highway crash. His father, Ralph Isham, filed a civil rights lawsuit against the officers on behalf of his son's estate, signing and submitting the complaint himself shortly before the two-year filing deadline expired.However, the US Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit has now revived the lawsuit, ruling that the initial filing could not automatically be treated as legally invalid after Isham hired an attorney. In its November 2, 2026, decision in Estate of Elijah Isham v. Richardson, available on Justia, the appeals court addressed whether a procedural violation involving legal representation could permanently invalidate an otherwise timely complaint.What happened during the fatal shootingThe incident began when police officers responded to a rollover vehicle crash on an interstate near Moraine, Ohio. They found Elijah Isham trapped inside an overturned car. Although he was badly injured, first responders reportedly saw him smoking methamphetamine and brandishing a gun from inside the vehicle. A standoff followed, during which officers fatally shot him.After his death, his father, Ralph Isham, became the administrator of his estate. He subsequently filed a federal civil rights lawsuit under 42 U.S.C. § 1983, alleging that the police chief and several officers involved in the incident had violated his son's Fourth Amendment rights. The Fourth Amendment protects individuals against unreasonable searches and seizures. Isham filed the complaint himself, just before the two-year statute of limitations expired.Why did the court question the father's filingThe district court raised concerns about whether Isham could represent his son's estate without an attorney. Under Section 1654 of Title 28 of the US Code, individuals can represent themselves in federal court but generally cannot represent another person's legal interests without being qualified lawyers. An exception applies to estate administrators who are the sole beneficiaries of an estate and whose estates have no creditors.The district court asked Isham to establish that he met both conditions or hire an attorney. He initially submitted a letter from the estate's probate attorney stating that no creditors had filed claims and that the period for doing so had expired. He also provided a document signed by Elijah's mother, indicating that she would not claim an interest in the proceeds of the federal lawsuit.However, the court found the documents insufficient to establish that Isham could represent the estate himself. It directed him to obtain legal representation or face dismissal. After receiving multiple extensions, Isham hired an attorney, who entered an appearance nearly a year after the original complaint was filed.Why was the lawsuit dismissed after he hired a lawyerThe defendants subsequently filed a motion to dismiss, challenging the lawsuit on grounds including improper service and failure to state a claim. They also argued that Isham's original complaint was invalid because he had filed it without being authorised to represent the estate. Their position was that hiring an attorney later could not correct the initial problem. The district court agreed, treating the original complaint as a legal nullity, meaning it should be considered as though it had never been filed.On September 26, 2025, the district court dismissed the lawsuit without prejudice. It rejected the defendants' service-related arguments but accepted their position concerning Isham's initial lack of legal representation. The estate sought reconsideration, submitting additional sworn statements from the probate attorney and Elijah's mother. However, the district court rejected the request, finding that the additional evidence could have been presented earlier.What did the Sixth Circuit decideThe Sixth Circuit examined whether a complaint filed by someone who cannot legally represent an estate without an attorney must automatically be treated as invalid, even if the person subsequently hires a lawyer. The appeals court considered differing approaches adopted by other federal appeals courts. While the Eighth Circuit had supported treating such complaints as legal nullities, the Eleventh Circuit had rejected that approach in a similar estate case. The Seventh Circuit had also recognised that courts could allow litigants to correct representation problems in cases involving corporate representation.The Sixth Circuit rejected the mandatory nullity rule. It held that district courts have discretion to decide how to address violations of Section 1654. They can set deadlines, strike filings or dismiss complaints when appropriate, but dismissal is not automatically required. In Isham's case, the district court had given him an opportunity to hire an attorney, and he complied within the prescribed timeline. The appeals court therefore concluded that he had corrected the representation problem and that his original complaint could not be dismissed as legally void simply because he had initially filed it without counsel.The court also rejected the defendants' argument that Ohio's law against unauthorised legal practice required the complaint to be treated as never filed. It clarified that federal law governs legal representation in federal court. The appeals court also rejected the defendants' argument under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 11(a), which requires pleadings to be signed by a party or their attorney. It noted that the rule allows signature defects to be corrected and that the defendants had raised the issue for the first time on appeal. The estate also said it intended to address it through an amended complaint.The Sixth Circuit reversed the dismissal and remanded the case for further proceedings. It also upheld the district court's refusal to reconsider its earlier decision based on additional evidence.What happens next?The ruling allows Elijah Isham's estate to continue pursuing its civil rights lawsuit against the police officers. However, the appeals court did not determine whether the officers used excessive force or violated Elijah's constitutional rights. It also did not award compensation to his estate.The decision specifically addresses the legal procedure surrounding the lawsuit. It clarifies that an initial filing made without authorised legal representation does not necessarily become invalid when the person subsequently hires an attorney within the timeline allowed by the district court.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ukraine raises death toll from Russian strike on Zaporizhia to 40 people
articles.summary: Dozens may still be under the rubble in Komyshuvakha. Rescue efforts ongoing despite interruptions by Russian drones.
articles.body:
Ukrainian authorities have raised the death toll from a Russian attack on an aid centre in the Zaporizhia region in the southeast of the country to 40 people.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced the raised toll on Wednesday, adding that some bodies had not yet been accounted for and that more than 30 people may still be under the rubble.

The strike on Monday was one of the deadliest strikes on civilians of Russia’s nearly five-year-long war on its neighbour. It came as Kyiv prepares to attend ceasefire talks with Moscow next week that have been brokered by the United States.

Local officials had earlier confirmed 37 deaths, adding that they estimate about 38 people could remain trapped following the attack, in which Russia dropped several bombs on a school building in the village of Komyshuvakha, near the front line, which was being used to distribute aid.

Ukraine said that a strike then hit an underground shelter filled with people in a follow-up attack. Four police officers and two members of a rescue crew were among the dead.

Zelenskyy condemned the “vile terrorist strike” and declared that it showed that Russia did not want de-escalation of the conflict. He added that the attack had wasted an opportunity created by a ceasefire and humanitarian mission last week in the front-line village of Oleshky.

Ukrainian police have released body-camera footage from one of the four officers killed, showing people being ushered into the underground shelter as the officer receives a radio warning of incoming guided aerial bombs.

People were then seen inside the shelter before the footage cuts to black and silence.

The United Nations human rights mission in Ukraine said on Tuesday that the bombing likely violated international law.

Local authorities said that Russian drones were hampering the search for victims in Komyshuvakha. Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of the regional military administration, insisted, however, that operations would continue.

The US has announced a new round of talks aimed at ending the war for next week. Special envoy Steve Witkoff has said delegations from Ukraine and Russia will meet in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 to discuss post-war security agreements, de-escalation, humanitarian measures and ending the war.

Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to the talks after meeting Witkoff in St Petersburg on October 21. However, previous such meetings have secured little progress, with Moscow refusing to compromise on hardline demands, including that Kyiv give up territory, demilitarise, and guarantee it will not seek to join NATO.

The Trump administration has appeared to offer support for Russia’s position, stoking concern in Kyiv and across Europe.

Zelenskyy has in the past sought to sway the US president by outlining the suffering of his country, and appeared to try to repeat the trick concerning the Zaporizhia atrocity.

“Unfortunately, there has been very little reaction from the world to this insane attack,” the Ukrainian president said in a social media post. “But it, like thousands upon thousands of other war crimes Russia has committed against Ukraine and Ukrainians, demands a strong response. Evil always goes further if it is left unanswered.”

articles.title: ‘Trump will be gone in two years’: Defeated Maine MAGA candidate Bobby Charles turns against president after election loss
articles.summary: A Republican candidate who modelled his campaign on US President Donald Trump has distanced himself from the president following a crushing defeat in
articles.body: A Republican candidate who modelled his campaign on US President Donald Trump has distanced himself from the president following a crushing defeat in Maine's gubernatorial election, saying he was optimistic about the future because Trump would be leaving office in two years.Bobby Charles, who lost to Democrat Hannah Pingree in Tuesday's election (November 3), made the remarks in an interview with Politico after his defeat."It sounds a little ironic," Charles said. "But I am nevertheless optimistic for the future because Trump's going to be gone in two years."Charles had promised to govern Maine along the lines of Trump's administration. At the launch of his gubernatorial campaign, he had said: "If you liked the first 90 days of Trump, if you liked the first two weeks of Trump, you would love the first few weeks of my administration, because we are going to flip this thing on its head."The Republican had also sold Trump-inspired merchandise on his campaign website and supported the president's tariffs and hardline immigration policies.He had actively sought Trump's endorsement during the campaign and welcomed Vice President JD Vance's backing, describing it as a "wonderful thing".Republicans blame Trump for election lossesCharles' remarks come as Republicans face a major setback in the 2026 midterm elections, with Democrats winning control of both chambers of Congress and several gubernatorial races.The losses have triggered criticism within the Republican Party, with some officials blaming Trump and his administration for the party's poor performance."We are beyond candidate quality. It's a bloodbath," a senior Senate Republican official told Politico, adding, "Trump did this."A Republican operative involved in swing-state campaigns also blamed the administration's handling of key issues."The people in the White House didn't do anything to stop him from engaging on things that were actively making everything worse because he was ignoring what the voters were caring about," the operative said.The criticism comes amid voter concerns over rising costs, inflation and the US conflict with Iran.White House rejects blameThe White House, however, has refused to accept responsibility for the Republican losses.A White House official told The Daily Beast that the administration remained "defiant", arguing that Trump was not personally on the ballot."President Trump was not on the ballot, and it's proven that Trump voters show up when he is on the ballot," the official said.The official also blamed the quality of candidates and predicted that voters who supported Democrats would regret their decision once gas prices declined following a resolution to the Iran conflict.Trump himself has dismissed suggestions that his leadership contributed to the Republican setback."I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE," he wrote on Truth Social.Vice President JD Vande posted a detailed analysis of the defeat. "The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," he concluded.Who is Bobby Charles?Charles, a Republican and former assistant secretary of state under President George W. Bush, contested the Maine gubernatorial election against Democrat Hannah Pingree and independent candidate Rick Bennett.Pingree, a former speaker of the Maine House of Representatives and daughter of Democratic Congresswoman Chellie Pingree, won the race.Charles had built his campaign around Trump's political agenda, particularly immigration enforcement. He had even proposed asking the White House to send Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents and US Marshals to Maine polling locations ahead of the midterm elections.His defeat comes as Democrats make significant gains across the country, turning the 2026 midterms into a major political setback for Trump and the Republican Party.You use AI every day. articles.title: 7 top-rated meat thermometers to end overcooked dinners, according to chefs
articles.summary: Make sure your chicken, beef and pork aren’t undercooked or overcooked by using one of these top-rated meat thermometers.
articles.body: This scenario might sound familiar. You’ve spent time in the kitchen cooking a wonderful meal. You plate everything up, but when you sit down and cut into your piece of meat, it’s totally overcooked — or, worse, raw. A meat thermometer may just be the answer to this culinary conundrum. “[Meat thermometers] let you know the internal temperature without cutting your protein open, which can dry your food out,” says Lauren Allen, chef and owner of Lauren Allen Dinners, which offers private chef experiences, virtual cooking classes and more. “That means your meat will be juicier and cooked to exactly your liking.” Adding this kitchen gadget to your repertoire doesn’t even have to cost you much — a good one can be found for under $20, says Allen. To help you shop for one of these handy tools, I spoke with two chefs to get their advice on what to look for when choosing a meat thermometer, and then I sourced top-rated options from popular retailers like Amazon, Walmart and Target. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter Top-rated meat thermometers Using expert advice, I selected digital meat thermometers from top retailers that have at least a 4-star average from at least 1,000 ratings. This thermometer has a two to three second read, according to the brand. This means it registers the internal temperature of meat that quickly. The LCD screen is backlit, which Alpha Grillers says makes it easy to read even in dim lighting. When not in use, the probe can be folded in to keep it clean and protected. Features of this thermometer include a three-to-five-second read time and the ability to read temperatures in Celsius or Fahrenheit. The rotating probe can be tucked in when not in use, and the back of the thermometer has a magnet on it so it can be hung on the side of your fridge. You can read temperatures in either Celsius or Fahrenheit with this digital thermometer, and the LCD screen displays the temperature in large numbers making it easier to read, according to the brand. The storage sleeve for the thermometer includes recommended internal temperatures for various proteins printed on it for reference. When folded, this thermometer fits in the palm of your hand. It comes in multiple colors, and only reads temperatures in Fahrenheit. The battery (LR44) is included, and it also has a carrying hole so you can hang it from a hook in your kitchen. This thermometer has a three to four second response, according to the brand, and you can switch between Celsius and Fahrenheit. Not only can you use it on meat, but you can also use it on liquids (for example, if you want to check the temperature of oil for frying). The back of the thermometer is magnetic so you can hang it on your fridge, and it comes in a variety of colors. This instant read thermometer has a three-second response and an LCD screen that lights up so you can read it even if the lighting is dim, according to the brand. This may be particularly helpful if you are grilling outdoors at dusk or sticking it in a dark oven. A reference guide of recommended internal temps for beef, poultry, pork and fish is printed right on the thermometer, and you can alternate between Celsius and Fareneheit. This thermometer has a read time of two to four seconds, according to the brand. The sides are textured to provide an anti-slip grip, and it has a magnetic back as well as a hanging loop. The backlit display allows you to read the temperature in the dark, and you can see the temperature in both Celsius and Farenheit. How to shop for a meat thermometer There are two common types of meat thermometers intended for in-home use. Probe thermometers stay in the meat the entire time it cooks. With instant read thermometers, you stick it into the meat to take the temperature and then remove it. Experts I spoke to prefer the instant read thermometers because they are easier to use and give fast, accurate temperatures. Here are some other features they suggest you consider: Digital read: There are both analog or digital meat thermometers on the market. “Digital is absolutely the way to go. They are faultless, assuming you don’t forget the batteries, and extremely quick to read,” says Kevin Gillespie, a chef with multiple James Beard nominations and culinary contributor at MeatEater, a site dedicated to cooking meat. Probe size: Allen and Gillespie both recommend paying close attention to the size of the probe (aka the prong you stick into the meat). “The larger the probe the more juices will flow out after you [test the temp],” says Allen. “You want the smallest hole possible, so look for a skinny probe.” Heat: You know what they say, if you can’t take the heat, get out of the kitchen — and that holds true for meat thermometers. Your oven, stovetop and grill can get hot, so you want to pick a thermometer that can handle high heat. “It should be able to withstand up to 250 degrees Fahrenheit,” says Allen. How to use a meat thermometer To get the right reading, follow these tips from Allen and Gillespie: Place your thermometer in the middle and thickest part of the protein and be sure to avoid hitting bone, says Allen. If you go to the thinnest area, it may tell you if that part is cooked but not the whole piece. Going for the center of the thickest part will ensure every part of whatever protein you are making is safe to eat. Take the thermometer out once you get your reading. Unlike probe thermometers, instant read thermometers are not intended to be left in a piece of meat. If you leave it in, you may melt the plastic it is encased in. Wash your thermometer after each use. To do this, just wipe down the probe with a little soap and water. Just take care not to immerse the entire thermometer in water. Though many thermometer’s claim to be waterproof, the digital display may not hold up to being submerged. What temperature should your meat be? Before you start cooking, it’s helpful to know the ideal temperature for whatever you are making. To help you out, the experts I spoke to recommend the following: Chicken: Poultry needs to be cooked to at least 165 degrees Fahrenheit, both Allen and Gillepsie say. Anything lower and you risk ingesting bacteria that can make you sick.Pork: “This is a bit of a hot topic. Some say it should be cooked to 165 degrees Fahrenheit. But if you buy good organic pork, 140 should be fine,” says Allen. Gillespie suggests 150 degrees Fahrenheit.Beef: If you’re cooking steak, it comes down to preference. For medium rare, cook your steak to 125 degrees Fahrenheit, says Allen. Prefer well done? You’ll want to bring it to 165 degrees Fahrenheit. Fish: The kind of fish will determine the right internal temperature. The general guideline for salmon is 145 degrees Fahrenheit, while snapper is done around 130 degrees Fahrenheit. Do your research on the type of fish you are cooking in advance, says Gillepsie. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. articles.title: Progressives fume at Hakeem Jeffries for saying Democrats won't 'get even' with Trump
articles.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Democrats should focus on lowering costs instead of getting even, but critics say accountability and delivering results go hand in hand.
articles.body: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., drew progressive criticism Wednesday after saying Democrats should focus on lowering costs following their midterm victories instead of getting "even" with the Trump administration. "The American people don't want us to get even; they want us to get things done on their behalf because life is way too expensive," Jeffries said on MS NOW's "Morning Joe." "We ran on affordability. We won on affordability, and now it's our job to govern on affordability." Many progressives want Democrats, now that they will have majorities in the House and Senate, to launch investigations into President Donald Trump, his family and government officials. Princeton historian Kevin Kruse criticized Jeffries, who is poised to become the next speaker of the House, while sharing a separate House Oversight Democrats post warning, "Lawyer up." HILLARY CLINTON WARNS DEMS MAY SQUANDER MIDTERM VICTORY IF THEY FAIL TO STAY FOCUSED AFTER ELECTION "As disheartening as Jeffries' comments were, remember that other House Democrats actually understand the moment and are ready to meet it," Kruse said in a Bluesky post. University of Michigan education professor Ebony Elizabeth Thomas also rejected Jeffries' framing, describing accountability as a matter of justice. "I say this with all love, Brother Leader Jeffries: No," Thomas said in a post responding to the clip. "And it's not (just) retribution. It's restorative justice." The Oversight Committee is expected to be chaired by Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., who was featured in the video put out by the committee's Democrats. Progressive commentator Brian Tyler Cohen said delivering for voters and investigating abuses of power should work together. "As content creators, we hear from huge, diverse audiences, and they all want the same thing: a government that works for them, lower costs, leaders who listen and accountability when people abuse their power," he said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "Delivering results and pursuing accountability go hand in hand, provided investigations follow the evidence and serve the public. "Creators helped people get involved in this election, and we're going to keep those conversations going, helping audiences stay informed and judge whether their elected leaders are delivering." ‘LAWYER UP’: DEMOCRATS, REPUBLICANS WASTE NO TIME IN SETTING SOCIAL MEDIA ABLAZE AFTER MIDTERM SWEEP The discussion followed Democrats' early warnings about using their anticipated investigative powers. Jeffries also addressed accountability during Wednesday's interview, saying Democrats should pursue facts, apply the law and follow the Constitution while holding wrongdoers responsible. In an August CNN interview, he identified the Judiciary and Oversight committees as taking the lead on accountability. He declined to rule impeachment in or out. "As we’ve done in the past, whenever there have been moments of accountability that we’ve had to lead on, we are guided by three principles: follow the facts, apply the law and be guided by the United States Constitution," Jeffries said. The White House said Trump remained willing to work with Democrats while criticizing the prospect of investigations targeting his administration. "As the president has said, he's willing to work with anyone to continue delivering victories for hardworking Americans. If Democrats choose to pursue sham investigations and radical left policies, they are choosing to work against the American people," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital. NEW YORK TIMES GLEEFUL OVER DEMOCRATS' HUGE MIDTERM VICTORIES, SAYS IT'S TIME TO ‘FEEL PRIDE’ A White House official separately warned that the administration retained federal powers as Democrats prepared to pursue investigations and subpoenas. "If crazed Democrats want to abuse their power and politicize their process of investigations, subpoenas and destroying lives, they should be reminded that we still control the federal government and all of its powers," the official said. Media Research Center President David Bozell separately criticized Democrats' campaign message and accused news organizations of shielding the party from scrutiny. "People want to talk about Trump defying norms? I think Democrats just defied a norm: They ran and won on … nothing," Bozell said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "The media aided and abetted. They were relentlessly negative. They refused to cover any good news. They buried every wart within Democrats' ranks. And today they will be right back at it." articles.title: A painting bought for around £500 at a British auction in 2024 was identified as an early work by JMW Turner; after authentication, The Rising Squall sold for nearly £1.9 million
articles.summary: An artwork that changed hands for little more than £500 at a regional British auction has turned into an extraordinary discovery in the art world.
articles.body: An artwork that changed hands for little more than £500 at a regional British auction has turned into an extraordinary discovery in the art world. The painting, initially believed to be the work of an artist associated with 18th-century painter Julius Caesar Ibbetson, was later identified as an early landscape by renowned British artist JMW Turner. Titled The Rising Squall, Hot Wells, from St Vincent's Rock, Bristol, the painting was eventually sold for approximately £1.9 million at Sotheby's in London in July 2025, after its attribution to Turner was established. The discovery was reported by The Guardian, The Art Newspaper and Artnet News, which followed the painting's journey from an overlooked auction lot to a major Old Master sale.A forgotten painting that resurfaced at a local auctionThe story began in April 2024, when the painting appeared at Dreweatts auction house in Newbury, England. It was catalogued as House by the Water in a Stormy Sky and attributed to a follower of Julius Caesar Ibbetson, rather than Turner himself. With no confirmed connection to a celebrated artist, the landscape attracted relatively little attention and sold for just £524.80, including fees.However, the buyer suspected that the painting might have been created by another artist, Philip James de Loutherbourg. During subsequent cleaning and restoration work, a signature reading W Turner was uncovered in the lower-left corner of the canvas. The discovery prompted further investigation into the painting's origins. Experts established its connection to Turner, with leading scholars supporting the attribution. What had appeared to be an ordinary 18th-century landscape was now recognised as an important early work by one of Britain's most celebrated painters.A rare glimpse into Turner's early artistic careerThe painting dates to around 1792, when Turner was just 17 years old. It depicts Hot Wells House, a former spa building near Bristol, positioned beside the River Avon against a dramatic landscape of turbulent water and approaching storm clouds.Its significance extends beyond its rediscovery. The work was Turner's first oil painting to be exhibited publicly, appearing at the Royal Academy in London in 1793, when the young artist was beginning to establish himself. Art historians have also noted the unusual way Turner approached the medium at this early stage. His use of delicate, translucent layers of oil paint gave parts of the composition a quality more commonly associated with watercolour.The landscape is particularly valuable because it offers an insight into the techniques and artistic ambitions that would later define Turner's celebrated treatment of light, weather and atmosphere.From a £500 purchase to a multimillion-pound auctionAfter the discovery, the painting was prepared for a much higher-profile appearance at Sotheby's Old Master and 19th Century Paintings evening sale in London on July 2, 2025. Ahead of the auction, it was estimated to fetch between £200,000 and £300,000. However, interest from collectors pushed the final price far beyond expectations.The painting sold for £1.5 million before auction fees, taking the final price to approximately £1.9 million. A private collector from the United Kingdom eventually secured the artwork after competition between multiple bidders. The result was particularly striking considering that the same painting had sold for just over £500 approximately 15 months earlier.Bristol makes an unsuccessful attempt to bring the painting homeThe auction also attracted considerable interest from Bristol, the city depicted in Turner's landscape. Bristol Museum and Art Gallery launched a public fundraising campaign called Bring Turner Home, hoping to acquire the painting and make it accessible to visitors. The appeal received more than £100,000 from over 1,700 contributors, allowing the museum to participate in the bidding. However, its offer was eventually surpassed by the winning private collector. Following the sale, the museum explored the possibility of securing the painting on loan so that it could still be displayed in the city connected to its subject. The painting's rediscovery also brought renewed attention to Turner's early connection with Bristol and the role the city played in his artistic development.What makes the story remarkable is not simply the difference between its two auction prices. It is the fact that a painting overlooked for generations, and misidentified when it finally resurfaced, turned out to be an important piece of British art history. A routine cleaning helped reveal its true identity, bringing a long-forgotten work from a private collection back into the public conversation.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Pound rises to its highest level since the Brexit referendum
articles.summary: Pound reaches highest level against a basket of currencies since the Brexit referendum a decade ago
articles.body:
The pound has risen to its highest overall level since the Brexit referendum over a decade ago.

Sterling has risen notably in recent weeks against the euro and the dollar, ahead of an expected rise in interest rates.

The most-watched measure of the value of the British currency against a basket of 18 of the world's main currencies this week reached its joint highest level since the June 2016 referendum, according to Bank of England figures.

The value reached 86.4 on an index where 100 equals the value in 2005. The Bank will officially confirm the calculation on Thursday.

The value of sterling fell significantly after the Brexit referendum in June 2016, and reached further lows during the Brexit process, the Covid pandemic and the 2022 mini-Budget.

Some traders said the UK was being seen in a different light given relative political stability, solid growth and the rapprochement with the European Union.

Sterling has responded strongly to Brexit developments and political uncertainty in recent years.

Jim O'Neill, an economist and former Treasury minister, said: "I'm not surprised. People were, and to a lesser extent, are, underestimating the improving momentum in the UK,"

A stronger pound can help rein in inflation, and increase buying power for consumers on imports and on holidays.

UK growth so far this year has outperformed all forecasts, but there are signs that higher energy and fuel prices have now hit consumer confidence.

The Bank's nine member Monetary Policy Committee faces an important decision on interest rates on Thursday, with the first rise in three years widely expected.

On Wednesday sterling was up 0.28% against the dollar at $1.3434 and was flat against the euro at €1.1996 as of 23:01 GMT.

articles.title: A Pennsylvania man spent four years making his sister's front lawn a Halloween destination; this October he unveiled a homemade 70-foot pirate ship, with costumed family members welcoming visitors for free
articles.summary: Discover how a Pennsylvania man dedicated four years to transforming his sister's lawn into a stunning Halloween destination featuring a massive 70-foot pirate ship. This community celebration includes costumed pirates, interactive displays, and a legacy of creativity that brings neighbors together every October.
articles.body: A Pennsylvania man's four-year effort to turn his sister's front lawn into a Halloween attraction has culminated in a 70-foot homemade pirate ship, complete with costumed characters welcoming visitors. The free display, built by Chris Clark with help from relatives and friends, has become an annual project at his sister's home in Broomall.Named the 'Miss Fortune', the ship is the latest addition to a series of themed Halloween installations Clark has created over the past four years. Visitors can walk through the display and interact with family members and friends dressed as pirates, who stay in character during Halloween celebrations.Clark began planning the ship in spring, with construction starting in early September. Speaking to 6ABC, he said the project was designed to bring people together and give the community a place to celebrate Halloween.Who is Chris Clark?Clark works as a business office manager at a local nursing home and previously spent 10 years as a wedding planner. He also studied theatre design and technology at DeSales University, a background that has informed his approach to building large-scale themed displays.His interest in Halloween decorations began when he was 12. What started in his basement gradually expanded into outdoor displays, including a walkthrough spread across more than an acre of property. He paused the tradition while attending college but wanted to revive it after graduating.His own home did not attract enough Halloween visitors, so his sister, Lisa Knox, and brother-in-law, Dan Knox, offered their front lawn as a venue. Clark began using the property about four years ago, with the family and their neighbours helping him bring each year's concept to life.From circus and western themes to a pirate shipThe 70-foot 'Miss Fortune' follows earlier installations based on a circus and a Western town. Clark's family, friends and neighbours contribute to the construction and help run the attraction, with visitors welcomed by people dressed in character.In a video interview with 6ABC, Clark said the ship took shape through months of preparation, beginning with sketches before the construction work started in September.The project has also become a shared activity for the neighbourhood. Lisa Knox said she sometimes returns from grocery shopping to find the scale of the installation at her home hard to believe. Another family member described the work as a team effort, with people from the community joining in as the display grows each year.What is HalloweenHalloween, also known as All Hallows' Eve, is observed on October 31 and has roots in the ancient Celtic festival of Samhain, which marked the transition from summer to winter around November 1. The Celts believed the boundary between the living and the dead became thinner during this period, prompting traditions such as lighting bonfires and wearing costumes to ward off spirits.The Christian church later designated November 1 as All Saints' Day, also known as All Hallows' Day, making October 31 All Hallows' Eve, a name that eventually became Halloween. European settlers brought these customs to America, where carved pumpkins replaced turnips as the material used for jack-o'-lanterns, helping shape the celebration as it is known today, according to the New York Public Library's account of Halloween history.You use AI every day.
