articles.title: Sudan factories struggle to restart after devastating wartime losses
articles.summary: War has left Sudanese workers jobless and consumers facing higher prices as factories struggle to reopen.
articles.body:
Khartoum, Sudan – Mansour Gaily’s factory in Khartoum produced sweets for local consumers and provided employment for workers.

But when fighting erupted between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in April 2023, production ground to a halt, like thousands of other businesses across the country.

More than three years later, Gaily faces the challenge of bringing his business back to life. Production may have resumed, but the factory is only operating at 40 percent of its previous capacity.

“Our losses are estimated at $1m,” Gaily told Al Jazeera. “We lost some machinery, spare parts, and needed to rebuild large parts of the factory.”

Gaily’s troubles are typical of Sudan’s devastated manufacturing sector . Before the war, Khartoum was one of the country’s main industrial centres, home to factories producing food, textiles and other consumer goods.

However, Khartoum became a major battleground between the SAF and the RSF during the war, and although there have only been sporadic attacks since the army fully recaptured it last year, the industrial sector has not been rebuilt.

According to Sudan’s Ministry of Industry, approximately 1,800 industrial facilities have been damaged during the war, including 650 factories that were completely destroyed.

The figures illustrate the scale of the challenge facing a sector that is essential to employment, domestic production and economic recovery.

Abdulelah Mohamed owns a factory for plastic products and recycling in Khartoum. He describes the situation as catastrophic.

“Damaging, destroying and looting the factories was systematic. We lost everything,” Mohamed said. “The industrial sector needs new planning and a new vision so Sudan can produce things again.”

The damage extends beyond buildings and machinery. Raw materials, finished goods and equipment have been destroyed or looted, while electricity shortages, damaged transport networks and rising import costs have made reopening difficult even for businesses whose premises survived the fighting.

Sara Elfatih Khalil, chief executive of Al Teital Advance Industries, is among the manufacturers confronting these challenges. Her company’s factory in Khartoum produced sesame oil and, before the war, provided employment for 300 workers. Its warehouses have been looted during the fighting, and with damaged buildings and a supply chain that remains broken, the factory continues to be shut down.

“I believe industry will remain a cornerstone of any economic recovery and that it is capable of recovering rapidly if the basic conditions are met,” Khalil said.

“Restoring our confidence as investors requires security and political stability, clear and consistent economic policies, legal protection for investment and property rights, and reliable financing and infrastructure,” Khalil said. “Our situation is not unique. Less than 10 percent of factories in the sector are currently operational, and those that remain open are operating intermittently, with costs that threaten their continued viability.”

For Gaily, restoring production at his sweets factory requires a steady supply of ingredients, including sesame and sugar, as well as packaging, spare parts, electricity and workers. Disruption to any of these can bring production to a halt.

“We are operating at 40 percent of our production capacity because the damage was severe and capital is limited,” he said. “Despite the lost spare parts and the lack of labourers, we chose to continue because we don’t have any other options.”

Other manufacturers face similar obstacles. Some now must import materials that were previously available locally, increasing costs and making production vulnerable to further disruptions in transport and supply.

The problems also extend to financing. Businesses that have lost machinery, stock and income during the war often lack the capital needed to replace equipment and pay for stock and employees before sales resume.

The consequences have extended to workers who depend on factories for their livelihoods.

Mohamed Haj is a worker who lost his job at a different sweets factory in Khartoum North and has struggled to find alternative employment.

“I lost my job at the beginning of the war, and the factory owner is unable to restore it,” Haj said. “Reviving the industrial sector in general could provide jobs for thousands of workers who have been left without work.”

At the other end of the supply chain, shopkeepers are struggling with the reduced availability of locally manufactured goods.

Abdelgadir Mohamed, who sells sweets and other consumer products in Bahri Central Market, said the disappearance of many Sudanese-made products has made it harder for traders to source stock.

“In some cases the imported products are cheaper for us and for the consumers,” the shopkeeper said, “but many of my customers prefer the Sudanese-made ones.”

Imports have partly filled the gap, but for shopkeepers this can mean higher purchasing costs and uncertain supplies, and for consumers already facing a decline in purchasing power, that adds pressure on household budgets.

“The prices are changing every day,” said Ahmed Mahmoud, a local consumer. “The local products’ prices are high and imported ones are also high, but for sweets like tahniya [a local sesame-based sweet], I prefer the Sudanese-made one.”

Sudanese authorities are now seeking to fix some of the damage. In August, a Ministry of Industry committee was established to assess the condition of industrial facilities in Khartoum State and prepare incentives to encourage factory owners to reopen. The recovery plan also includes restoring essential services in industrial areas, including electricity, water, roads, sewage and waste management.

The services are critical for manufacturers hoping to resume operations, but factory owners say reconstruction would require more than just restoring infrastructure.

Many factory owners need capital, and representatives of the Sudanese Chamber of Commerce say businesses need real, practical assistance, rather than just promises from authorities.

Economist Mohamed Elnayer believes reconstruction offers an opportunity to address longstanding weaknesses in Sudan’s industrial economy.

“Rebuilding the industrial sector will require a broader strategy that addresses the structural weaknesses that existed even before the war,” Elnayer said.

Before the war, Khartoum was the industrial heart of Sudan, with the country’s factories largely concentrated inside it. That caused an inequality in opportunities between Khartoum and the rest of the country before the war, but a different problem arose during the conflict, when the capital became a major front line.

Many factories were destroyed and looted as a result, and analysts like Elnayer believe that the industrial sector should be rebuilt across Sudan. This would serve the dual purpose of avoiding any future paralysis of the industrial sector if fighting were to break out in the capital again, and also spread economic benefits around the country.

“Sudan needs to consider, before reconstruction, whether to simply restore the industrial sector that existed before the conflict, or provide an opportunity to develop a more competitive and productive economy in other Sudanese states,” he added.

For Gaily, those broader economy questions are inseparable from the practical challenge of keeping his factory running.

He hopes to repair the machinery, secure the ingredients needed to manufacture sweets and bring his former employees back.

“We need stronger support from the authorities by facilitating production, rehabilitating infrastructure and adopting stronger policies to encourage factory owners,” Gaily said. “Above all, the industrial sector needs financial support and coordinated efforts by stakeholders to sustain economic recovery.”

articles.title: In season of protests, contentious Agnipath provision rolled back to send message to youth
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In a season when the young have hogged political conversations, govt's move to roll back the contentious provision of Agnipath scheme by
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a season when the young have hogged political conversations, govt's move to roll back the contentious provision of Agnipath scheme by opening a pathway to permanent jobs addresses a core concern of millions of aspirants. For them, entry into the forces was a ticket to social mobility, and the provision allowing only 25% of Agniveers to be absorbed after four years was a source of resentment.Coming ahead of a crucial round of assembly polls, including in UP, Uttarakhand and Punjab - key states for recruitment in the forces - the BJP-led NDA govt will hope the decision placates the youth.Though the govt had said at the scheme's rollout in 2022 that it was open to reviewing it, especially percentage of Agniveers to be absorbed permanently, it took its time to make amendments despite opposition attacks. It unveiled them amid its rivals' campaign over SIR and efforts to bring Gen Z into their ranks.The move fits BJP's strategy of not appearing to cede ground to rivals but changing course to address concerns of its audience when the opposition seems to have moved on.Govt similarly decided to conduct a caste census in 2025, a demand raised by the opposition ahead of 2024 LS elections, as it became clear that a large section of OBCs, whom BJP has courted and successfully, were sympathetic to the idea.The development has now triggered speculation in political circles over whether govt will also rethink the contentious anti-discrimination UGC guidelines, which upset general castes as they were perceived to project them as likely oppressors and others as likely victims on campuses. The guidelines issued have been stayed by SC. Govt has since maintained silence on its stand, saying only that it supports justice and fairness on campuses.It is tricky terrain for BJP. It will not want to antagonise its core general-caste constituents further, but cannot afford to let down the backward classes, much larger in number and crucial to its fortunes in UP.A vocal section of general castes, especially youths, continues to criticise BJP on social media for allegedly cultivating OBCs, SCs and STs while ignoring the sentiments of its original flag-bearers.

articles.title: ‘For me, it’s relaxing’: Trump boasts White House ballroom after Republican wipeout in midterms
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Wednesday turned the spotlight on the construction of his under-construction White House ballroom during his first public
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Wednesday turned the spotlight on the construction of his under-construction White House ballroom during his first public appearance after Republicans suffered sweeping losses in the midterm elections, spending much of the event showcasing his renovation projects rather than addressing the party's electoral setback.Trump assembled reporters and construction workers at the unfinished structure as the final steel beam was prepared to be hoisted into the ballroom's roof.He praised the project's design, construction quality and security features, describing the planned addition as one of the most beautiful ballrooms in the world."This is a special structure. It's going to be not only one of the biggest, but it'll be the most beautiful ballroom I think anywhere in the world," he was quoted as saying by CBS News.According to Reuters, Trump defended his focus on the construction work, saying the White House was the "ultimate symbol of America" and needed to be maintained to the highest standards."When I get criticized, like, 'Why are you working on the White House?' I'm doing it because the White House is the ultimate symbol of America, and it's got to be pristine, it's got to be perfect. For me it's relaxing," he said.Trump also spoke about plans to install Corinthian columns inside the ballroom and said marble had been ordered for its flooring.He further highlighted other projects, including a new White House helipad, a proposed Garden of American Heroes along the Potomac River and plans for an 18-hole championship golf course at East Potomac Park, the New York Post reported.The president signed his name on the final steel beam, adding the word "Love!" before workers raised it into position.Trump acknowledges Iran war contributed to GOP lossesWhile Trump eventually addressed the election results, he rejected the idea that he was responsible for the Republican Party's poor performance. Democrats made significant gains in both chambers of Congress, securing control of the Senate and the House of Representatives.However, Trump acknowledged that the US war with Iran, which contributed to higher energy prices and inflation, played a role in the Republican setback."I think it's largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term," he said, agreeing with Vice President JD Vance's assessment of the election outcome.Trump, however, defended the military campaign, saying he would make the same decision again because Iran could not be allowed to develop nuclear weapons.He also appeared unfazed by the prospect of dealing with Democratic majorities in Congress, saying he expected to get along with them unless they chose to be "destructive". "But I have the power of the veto," he added.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Democratic Socialists of America see record wins in US midterm elections
articles.summary: The left-wing movement has won support for its views on issues like the war in Gaza and universal healthcare.
articles.body:
A record number of candidates for federal offices who were backed by or affiliated with the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) won in Tuesday’s US midterm elections, marking the most successful night the left-leaning movement has had in national politics so far.

“This is a record for the DSA; these are numbers we have not seen in over a hundred years in socialist electoral activity,” National Electoral Commission member Chanpreet Singh said on a livestream on Tuesday night after the elections. The stream, broadcast on Twitch to more than 200,000 viewers, was hosted by political commentator Hasan Piker.

The political group saw a surge in membership in 2016, when Vermont’s US Senator Bernie Sanders, a prominent DSA member, ran unsuccessfully for president, bringing the movement’s views on issues like universal healthcare and housing to a broader audience. The election of Zohran Mamdani as mayor of New York City in 2025 brought more attention, and more members, to the DSA.

Today the movement says it has more than 120,000 members, with chapters across all 50 states. Members vote to decide which candidates to back in elections, in federal contests like those for the US Congress, as well as state and local bodies. Many of the candidates that the DSA endorses share views on core issues, including the war in Gaza, healthcare, and immigration.

So where did DSA-affiliated candidates win federal offices on November 3?

In New York State, three candidates who were either officially endorsed by the chapter or were closely affiliated with the DSA were elected to office on Tuesday: Claire Valdez, Darializa Avila Chevalier, and Brad Lander were elected to the US House of Representatives for the first time, and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez was re-elected to her seat. Chevalier, who worked on Mamdani’s mayoral campaign, has helped organise pro-Palestinian protests and has been vocal about her opposition to Israel’s war on Gaza.

In Michigan, DSA member Rashida Tlaib was re-elected to her seat in the US House, member Donavan McKinney was elected to the body for the first time, and William Lawrence defeated a Republican candidate for a highly competitive US House seat.

Melat Kiros, a 29-year-old immigrant from Ethiopia who has also been outspoken on her views on issues like opposing Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza and abolishing US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), was elected to office with a wide margin to represent Colorado in the House.

In Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, voters elected Chris Rabb, a former state lawmaker, to the US House for the first time.

On the West Coast in Los Angeles, California, Angela Gonzales-Torres defeated a Democratic incumbent for a seat in the US House.

Adam Hamawy, a former US Army medical doctor who has worked as a surgeon in Gaza, won a district in New Jersey. Although he is not a DSA member, he has aligned himself with the movement and campaigned alongside DSA-backed candidates.

There was once a time when Legos in general symbolized the ultimate Christmas or birthday gift for children, but today Lego sets make some of the best holiday gifts for people in all stages of life, whether heading to junior high or opening up a Roth IRA. What makes them so giftable is that, aside from the fact that each set comes in an easy-to-wrap, lightweight rectangular box, Legos are available in seemingly endless themed options that speak to people’s passions and various personalities, nostalgic media and timeless hobbies. Additionally, I’ve included Lego products that aren’t sets but are equally as popular, like the Lego Brick Box. Many of the sets and Lego items below are categorized by age, but if you’re an adult, you can definitely choose any that sound fun. Plus, if you need extra convincing, many of these Lego sets are frequently on sale on Amazon and other retailers like Target and Walmart. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date. I included a number of Lego Duplo sets since the Duplo blocks are simple to use and much larger than regular Lego pieces, making them best for small children. Each set listed below is also highly-rated, with at least a four-star rating from customer reviews on Amazon and other retailers. It’s perfect for the person who loves the interactivity of building it, either by themselves or with another person, and wants something to display on an entryway, bedside, dining or coffee table. I bought this Lego set last year and gave it to a family member who still has it displayed in her living room today. It’s a super affordable set that makes for great decor. I also love that each Lego set comes in a small box that’s easy to cover with wrapping paper — plus, they fit in my suitcase easily. It’s suitable for all ages, and it’s a great set to help give your work or home a little more whimsy at a low price. Best Lego gifts for ages 2+ Toddlers fascinated by construction vehicles will find a lot to enjoy in this Lego Duplo set. This set includes four animal figures, grass and ice blocks for imitating a natural habitat. Pair it with the Lego Duplo Animals at the Farm set for even more imaginative animal play. Best Lego gifts for ages 4+ This is one of the best Lego gifts if you’re looking to start or bolster someone’s Lego collection. This Bluey set includes the titular character, plus Chloe and a buildable playground with a tower, slide, seesaw and pelican ride. Best Lego gifts for ages 5+ A monster truck easily fits into any Lego collection — huge rubber tires and blue flame decals help this one stand out. Best Lego gifts for ages 6+ This three-in-one set can be built into a space shuttle, spaceship or astronaut figure. The set includes a baseplate and accessories, making it easy to adjust or rearrange the scenery to your liking. Mario is not just a video game character, he’s in movies, theme parks and Lego sets. Best Lego gifts for ages 7+ This is a three-in-one set: there are pieces and instructions to build either a tyrannosaurus rex, triceratops or pterodactyl. Best Lego gifts for ages 8+ The centerpiece of this magical set is the Hogwarts Express train: it has a movable engine, coal and passenger cars, and it has room to fit and pose various minifigures and accessories. Plus, it includes the Hogsmeade train station and eight minifigures, including Harry, Ron, Hermione and Hagrid. Best Lego gifts for ages 9+ Lego Technic sets have more intricate pieces than other sets, and are often used to make accurate models of vehicles like cars, planes and motorbikes. This model of the Lamborghini Huracan Tecnica has details like a V10 engine, opening car doors and wheel steering. The finished car is about 11 inches long and 4.5 inches wide. The titular Stitch (from “Lilo and Stitch”) stands at more than eight inches tall and has movable ears and a turnable head for easy posing. He comes with his Hawaiian shirt, plus accessories like an ice-cream cone and flower. Play with changing moods using this Lego set featuring Joy and Anxiety from the movie “Inside Out 2.” The set has two buildable cubes and nine mood plates that can easily be arranged and rearranged on the cubes. It also has a buildable display stand with a small control board, just like in the movie. This 25-inch-by-20-inch puzzle depicts 78 minifigures, and is a great way for puzzle-lovers and Lego-lovers to get together in play. It is a jigsaw-style puzzle full of fun and goofy characters. Best Lego gifts for ages 10+ “Star Wars” fans of all ages can find something to love in this R2-D2 set. The droid has a rotating head that can swivel all the way around, wheels to move with, and small details like an attachable periscope and tools. You can bring the battle offline with this Fortnite set that includes a flying battle bus, nine minifigures and tools for your giftee to use for imaginative play. You can slot figures inside the bus, which also has a detachable balloon. This Ferrari SF-24 F1 race car has plenty of detail for fans of sports car figurines. The set includes a red race car, an F1 driver minifigure and team and sponsor logos. This mega-sized minifigure is 10.6-inches tall — it makes regular minifigures look like ants by comparison. It has a movable head, arms, legs and hands, but it also has an opening hat. Inside, there is a regular-sized minifigure that appears to be piloting the mega-sized one. Best Lego gifts for ages 12+ Lego Architecture sets recreate landmarks from around the world — this one includes iconic Paris buildings like the Eiffel Tower, Louvre and Arc de Triomphe. The completed set is about 11 inches wide and eight inches tall, compact enough for desks or nightstands. Best Lego gifts for ages 18+ This detailed Lego set recreates Wonka’s chocolate factory from the 1971 movie, with a chocolate waterfall, Wonkatania boat, Willy Wonka’s office and more. It also includes nine minifigures of characters like Willy Wonka, Charlie Bucket and Augustus Gloop, to name a few. Remember the lamp bouncing on the ball at the start of every Pixar movie? That’s Luxo Jr., recreated in detail with this Lego set. The lamp has multiple hinges and joints, so you can adjust its height, swivel, tilt, rotation and positioning, and it includes a buildable ball to recreate the bounce from the short film. Best Lego accessory gifts Organize your Lego pieces, or anything else, using this plastic drawer in the shape of a four-studded Lego block. It stacks with other four-studded Lego storage bricks, so you can build out a drawer-system to your liking. This small, soft pouch is best for carrying non-Lego items — think school supplies, chargers, makeup, anything you might put in a small zip bag. It has one large zippered compartment and two smaller, stud-shaped ones on the top. These organizer cubes can store Lego bricks or anything else that needs to be sorted and sealed. Each cube has a zipper closure and a see-through top so you can easily grab what’s inside with a quick glance. The smaller red and blue cubes fit inside the larger yellow one, if all three are empty. articles.title: El Nino is making the Pacific 'burn with fever', triggering typhoon after typhoon in East Asia
articles.summary: Even for countries where typhoons are a way of life, the last few months have brought unusually wild weather.
articles.body:
Wild weather is a way of life for people living along the coast in the Philippines, Taiwan, China and Japan. But the last few months have been extraordinary.

A wave of intense and, at times, unpredictable storms exacerbated by the El Niño weather pattern has killed dozens, shuttered major airports and wiped out crops and infrastructure across a swathe of East Asia.

In October, nearly all of Taiwan shut down as a monster storm big enough to engulf the island of 23 million roared towards its north-eastern coast. Equivalent to a category five hurricane, Typhoon Champi's 295km/h (193mph) winds had the power to flatten homes and whip up destructive waves.

Thankfully it did not make landfall in Taiwan, skirting past the island while dousing it in rain. But it had far-reaching impacts : hundreds of flights were cancelled in Hong Kong, Taiwan and Japan. In the Philippines' Batanes archipelago, seaside highways shut as huge waves crashed onto the shore, and in southern Japan's Okinawa islands, power was cut to 15,000 homes.

El Niño is a naturally occurring climate phenomenon in which warm waters pooling in the eastern Pacific and altered wind patterns drive extreme weather events around the world.

It happens around every two to seven years, lasting for around a year. This year's El Niño, which the UK Met Office has forecast to be the "strongest in living memory", is likely to last until February or March.

In June, Japan watched two storms - Typhoon Mekkhala and Severe Tropical Storm Higos - race towards its eastern coast simultaneously, forcing one million people to evacuate. In July, Tropical Storm Narra grazed China's southern coast along Guangxi, submerging villages and displacing tens of thousands.

August brought Super Typhoon Dolphin, which churned across the Pacific for 16 days - before slamming into eastern China, triggering heavy floods and dozens of casualties .

Later that month Typhoon Saudel made landfall in three south-eastern Chinese cities over one week, shutting transport networks and forcing thousands to evacuate.

The Pacific Ocean, heated to record levels by El Niño, is now brimming with typhoon energy, according to the Accumulated Cyclone Energy (ACE) metric which measures the total intensity of a season's storms. This year, the ACE reading for South East and East Asia is forecast to be nearly double the 30-year average.

El Niño also affects wind patterns and in this case, that means typhoons are tending to form further east than usual. They are also becoming stronger as they remain over warm waters for longer.

The Pacific can be likened to someone "burning with fever", says Ana Liza Solis, head of climatology at the Philippines' national weather bureau. "It can go into convulsions soon," she said at a press briefing in Manila in September.

Forecasts suggest the worst may not be over. Last month, sea surface temperatures in the equatorial Pacific - the area monitored by the Japan Meteorological Agency for its El Niño predictions - soared to 4C above normal, the highest since records began in 1949. The previous record - 3.6C - was set in December 1997.

China's climate agency has warned of sea surface temperatures continuing to rise over the next three months because of the El Niño.

Despite typhoon season usually peaking around September to October, this is likely to raise concerns across a region that has already been battered by back-to-back storms.

In August, Typhoon Chan-Hom baffled storm watchers in Japan by crossing the country from east to west, as opposed to the usual south-to-north trajectory. Japan's well-resourced and prepared authorities were able to evacuate people swiftly, but this would be far more challenging in some neighbouring countries.

To get a better picture of how rising temperatures could amplify the risks, Manila-based climatologist Rafaela Jane Delfino and colleagues simulated the effects of warmer conditions on the Philippines' most recent monster storms, including 2013's Super Typhoon Haiyan (Yolanda) which killed more than 6,000 people.

They arrived at what she describes as "very, very scary findings": higher temperatures increased total accumulated rainfall by 26%. It's a devastating prospect in a country where flooding from monsoon rains and some 20 tropical storms per year has emerged as one of the main disaster risks.

In recent years, floods have paralysed entire cities for days, and tired of the annual ordeal, Filipinos have taken to the streets to protest against corruption which they say is gnawing away at millions of dollars from flood-control projects.

Delfino, in an article on the University of the Philippines website, insists leaders and officials must gain a better understanding of climate hazards if communities are to be better prepared.

Countries are bracing for the immediate impact. Japan has urged citizens to stockpile food and essentials for the typhoon season , and to secure outdoor furniture that could become deadly projectiles when typhoon winds hit. China has asked local officials to identify vulnerable areas and is upgrading its warning and monitoring systems.

The Philippines and its South East Asian neighbours are preparing for disruptions to food production, especially rice, and have increased support for famers, including the provision of fertilisers.

But what happens in the long term is less clear. The window for governments to act on El Niño is "closing", the United Nations Development Programme in Asia and the Pacific said recently.

"How severely a community experiences an El Niño is decided years in advance, by where roads and settlements are built, how water is managed, who is covered by social protection and whether public budgets have room to absorb a shock.

"Every El Niño tests the resilience we have built; this one should also drive us to build more," it added.

articles.title: Prez can be prosecuted after leaving office but not ECs, says petitioner
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has tagged two petitions challenging Section 16 of Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions
articles.body: The Supreme Court has tagged two petitions challenging Section 16 of Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, with a pending plea raising a similar issue. The provision bars courts from entertaining or continuing civil or criminal proceedings against serving or former CECs and election commissioners for acts done or purported to be done in discharge of official duties.A bench told lawyers for Manoj Jha and Arun Agrawal that the cases would be tagged with the pending matter.Jha's plea argues that Section 16 gives officials wider protection than President, MPs, and SC and HC judges, covering civil and criminal proceedings during tenure and for life, without exceptions for corruption, mala fides or crime. It says President may be prosecuted after leaving office, while a former election commissioner arguably cannot."A member of Parliament who takes a bribe to vote can be tried but an EC who takes a bribe while "purporting" to act in office arguably cannot. A sitting judge of this court can be prosecuted with sanction yet a retired election commissioner cannot be prosecuted with or without it. The Constitution places no functionary above the law, however Section 16 of the CEC does," the plea said.Agrawal's plea said the wording "is or was" creates lifelong immunity, while "purporting to act" could cover conduct outside lawful authority. It said the provision contained no good-faith condition and could bar prosecution for corruption, forgery and other serious offences.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: JACKSON THOMPSON: Democrat-appointed judges hand Letitia James win over county trying to protect girls sports
articles.summary: A four-judge panel found Nassau County's transgender athlete ban conflicts with New York's Human Rights Law, but the county vows to appeal it.
articles.body: A New York appeals court Wednesday struck down Nassau County’s law barring transgender girls and women from women’s sports teams using county facilities, handing Attorney General Letitia James a victory in her legal battle with Bruce Blakeman. The unanimous ruling by a four-judge panel of the Appellate Division, Second Department, reversed a lower-court decision upholding the restrictions. The judges found that the county law conflicted with New York’s statewide antidiscrimination protections. Nassau County Attorney Thomas Adams indicated the county would continue fighting. "We are reviewing the decision with the intention to continue the appeals process," Adams said in a statement. The decision came one day after Blakeman lost his gubernatorial challenge to Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul. James also won reelection Tuesday. All four judges who joined the ruling were elevated to the appellate court by Democratic governors. Former Gov. Andrew Cuomo appointed Justice Betsy Barros in April 2014 and Justice Deborah Dowling in June 2021. Hochul appointed Justice Barry Warhit in May 2022 and announced Justice Lisa Ottley’s selection earlier this year. State election records list Barros, Dowling and Warhit as Democratic candidates in their judicial election histories. Ottley ran for state Supreme Court in 2018 on the Democratic, Republican and Conservative ballot lines, according to New York City’s official voter guide. 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS' LEGAL DEFENSE AND TRANS ATHLETE'S ATTORNEYS SPEAK OUT AFTER LANDMARK SCOTUS RULING The appeals court held that Nassau’s permit restrictions were preempted by the state Human Rights Law and Civil Rights Law, which prohibit discrimination based on gender identity or expression. It directed the lower court to enter a judgment declaring the measure invalid under the state Constitution and Municipal Home Rule Law. "Nobody should have to fight to play the game they love. Transgender athletes have the right to play on the court, field, or roller rink like everyone else, and today the Second Department made clear that Nassau County cannot ban them," James said in a statement. "No one asked for this illegal and exclusionary policy. Bruce Blakeman was just trying to stop athletes from playing with their teammates. I am pleased the court saw right through it." The county law required organizations seeking permits for sporting events at county facilities to designate themselves as male, female or coed based on biological sex at birth. It prohibited permits for female events that allowed male competitors, while permitting female athletes in male and coed categories. The restrictions did not prohibit transgender athletes from all sports participation. They prevented teams designated for women or girls from obtaining county permits if they included transgender female competitors. The measure affected more than 100 county facilities, including athletic fields, basketball and tennis courts, swimming pools and ice rinks, according to James’ office. INSIDE THE SUPREME COURT BATTLE TO 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS' Blakeman first imposed the policy through a February 2024 executive order. After a judge struck down that order on the grounds that he lacked authority to issue it, the county Legislature passed legislation reinstating the restrictions. Blakeman signed the law July 15, 2024, prompting separate lawsuits from James and the New York Civil Liberties Union. The NYCLU represented the Long Island Roller Rebels, an adult women’s roller derby league that welcomes transgender participants. State Supreme Court Justice R. Bruce Cozzens upheld the law in October 2025, accepting the county’s safety and fairness arguments and reasoning that transgender athletes could participate in coed leagues. The county also argued that Title IX supported its use of biological sex to separate athletic categories. However, the Second Department separately granted the Roller Rebels a preliminary injunction in October 2025, reversing Cozzens’ earlier refusal to temporarily block enforcement. NEWSOM FACES CRITICISM FOR STATE'S STANCE ON TRANS ATHLETES IN GIRLS' SPORTS AFTER SCOTUS RULING In that decision, the appeals court found that limited access to private facilities had reduced the league’s practice opportunities and hurt its ranking. It also found that requiring the league to identify as mixed-sex could jeopardize its governing-body status and ability to find opponents. The litigation unfolded alongside a broader national fight over transgender eligibility in female sports. In June, the U.S. Supreme Court upheld the challenged restrictions in West Virginia and Idaho, concluding that schools could determine eligibility for female teams by biological sex under Title IX and the Equal Protection Clause. That ruling permitted the challenged state policies; it did not require every state to adopt such restrictions. Nassau’s case instead turned on whether the county could impose a permit policy that conflicted with New York state law. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. articles.title: A rare silver coin pattern made in London around 1867 for trade in Shanghai spent decades in a private collection; it has now sold for $4.758 million at a Hong Kong auction, leading a nearly $32 million sale
articles.summary: A silver coin designed more than 150 years ago for a proposed international trading currency has fetched $4.758 million at an auction in Hong Kong,
articles.body: A silver coin designed more than 150 years ago for a proposed international trading currency has fetched $4.758 million at an auction in Hong Kong, despite never becoming part of regular circulation. Made in London around 1867-68, the rare Kwan Ping Trade Coinage pattern was intended to be part of a proposed Chinese-Foreign Circulating Coin series. The coin had remained out of public view for decades after entering a private collection in the mid-20th century. According to auction house Stack's Bowers Galleries, it became the highest-selling lot at its October 2026 Hong Kong auction, which generated nearly $32 million in total sales.The coin, officially catalogued as the silver 'Chinese-Foreign Circulating Coin' Tael Pattern, was sold as Lot 41023. It was graded PCGS Specimen-66, a designation reflecting its exceptional preservation and specimen-quality striking. The auction concluded on October 26, with the results announced on November 3. The final price of $4,758,000 included the buyer's premium.A proposed currency that never reached circulationThe story of the coin goes back to a period when international trade involving China faced difficulties because different regions and trading communities used varying monetary systems and standards. Foreign merchants operating through Chinese treaty ports had to navigate a complicated monetary environment, creating interest in a more uniform silver currency that could be recognised across trading markets.The proposed Kwan Ping series was part of efforts to develop such a standard. Its design was proposed by W. F. Wade, the Chinese Secretary of the British Legation in Peking. According to the original auction catalogue, Wade's proposal was communicated on October 19, 1867, through Captain Kinder to the Governor of Hong Kong.The plan involved producing coins according to the Maritime Customs weight scale, with five denominations: one tael, five mace, two mace, one mace and five candareens. These denominations were intended to make the coins useful for wider commercial transactions rather than limiting them to a single local market.Although the designs were produced in England, the intention was for the coins to be manufactured for circulation through the Hong Kong Mint. However, the project did not progress as planned. The Hong Kong Mint closed in April 1868, and its machinery was subsequently sold to the Osaka Mint in Japan. The proposed currency never developed into a regular circulating coinage.Why the coin remained a mystery for decadesOne reason the Kwan Ping pattern is particularly valuable to collectors is the uncertainty that surrounded its origins and intended use. For years, numismatic researchers debated whether the coins had been manufactured in Berlin, London or Osaka. Their unusual designs also led to suggestions that they might have been intended for trade with Korea.The original auction catalogue credits research by numismatic scholar Joe Cribb, particularly his reference work Money in the Bank, with establishing the English origin of the dies and patterns. The dies were deposited at the Royal Mint in London in 1888 by the heirs of Captain Kinder. Original design drawings and correspondence relating to the proposed coinage also survive in London.The catalogue further refers to archival documents and correspondence discovered in 2017-18 that helped establish the production and shipment history of the series. A letter dated December 31, 1875, from Peter Campbell to Sir Robert Hart, Inspector-General of China's Imperial Maritime Customs Service, recorded that sample coins had been dispatched to banking agents in Shanghai and Yokohama on December 17. A separate box containing 100 samples of each denomination was sent from Southampton, England, on December 30.The records suggest that only 102 examples of each denomination were produced, making the series exceptionally scarce. The discovery also helped clarify that the coins were likely intended for wider international trade rather than exclusively for commerce with Korea.The design itself reflects the cultural influences behind the proposed currency. The coin features two intertwined Chinese-style dragons surrounding a yin-yang symbol on one side. The opposite side carries inscriptions indicating its denomination, accompanied by decorative branches. A small anchor appears in the outer border of the dragon side, serving as a mintmark.The name Kwan Ping is associated with the weight standard used for the proposed trade coinage. The auction catalogue identifies the particular specimen as a one-tael pattern. Its unusual combination of Chinese imagery and British production history makes it an important piece for collectors studying the development of Asian currency.A coin kept away from the market for 76 yearsThe specimen that recently sold belonged to the Liu Mung Wang Collection, a private collection that had remained largely unavailable to the market for more than half a century. According to the auction catalogue, the coin was acquired by Liu Mung Wang directly from his longtime friend and fellow high-school classmate, H. Chang, a noted Chinese numismatist of the early and mid-20th century. The transaction took place before the coin disappeared from the public auction market in 1950.It had remained outside the market for approximately 76 years before being offered at the October 2026 sale. The auction house described the specimen as previously unrecorded, adding to its significance among surviving examples of the series. The coin's PCGS Specimen-66 grade also reflects its remarkable state of preservation.Rare Chinese coins lead nearly $32 million auctionThe Kwan Ping pattern was not the only Chinese coin to attract significant attention at the Hong Kong auction. Five coins crossed the million-dollar mark, with several other historical silver patterns also achieving substantial prices.According to Stack's Bowers, the second-highest-selling lot was a 1929 Chinese silver dollar pattern from the Tientsin Mint, graded PCGS Specimen-63, which fetched $2.074 million. A 1927 silver dollar pattern from the same mint sold for $1.891 million.Two other notable results included a 1911 silver Large-Tailed Dragon dollar pattern, which realised $1.22 million, and a 1903 silver tael pattern, struck using Osaka Mint dies, which sold for $1.098 million. All five million-dollar coins belonged to the Chinese numismatic category.The auction featured more than 7,400 lots and recorded a sell-through rate exceeding 94%, generating nearly $32 million in total realised prices. More than $2 million worth of banknotes also changed hands, including historical Chinese currency and notes from other countries.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: CBB With Danny Z: Kansas, Tennessee and USC lead another human polls vs. analytics argument
articles.summary: Kansas ranks outside the AP top 15 but fifth in KenPom, highlighting major splits among four college basketball ranking systems this preseason.
articles.body: College basketball is back, and so is "CBB With Danny Z." Try to contain your excitement (I'm genuinely psyched that college hoops is back, but I understand that many people don't even realize college basketball exists until February or March). Last season, we kicked off a series comparing the preseason AP Top 25 with KenPom's rankings, then checked back in December, January and March to see how those disagreements developed. UCONN BASKETBALL COACH FLOATS POTENTIAL GAME AT WHITE HOUSE AFTER UFC EVENT KenPom deserves some credit for Vanderbilt last season. It ranked the Commodores 19th in the preseason, while the AP voters had them effectively 36th. Vanderbilt finished 27-9, earned a No. 5 seed and won an NCAA Tournament game. But KenPom also had Baylor 17th in the preseason. The Bears finished 17-17 and missed the tournament. St. John’s was a reminder to be careful about declaring a winner in December. The AP’s preseason No. 5 team started 4-3, which initially made KenPom’s more cautious ranking of 16th look pretty smart. Then the Red Storm finished 30-7, reached the Sweet 16 as a No. 5 seed and pushed Duke in an 80-75 loss. The voters’ optimism looked considerably more reasonable by the end of the season. The AP voters had their own problems with Creighton. They put the Bluejays 23rd in the preseason, while KenPom had them all the way down at 41st. Creighton finished 16–18 and missed the NCAA Tournament, settling for a trip to the College Basketball Crown. I’m guessing that wasn’t the postseason tournament those voters had in mind. So, there’s a reason to keep track of these disagreements. This year, we’re giving ourselves a few more to follow. Alongside KenPom, I’m adding TeamRankings’ predictive ratings to the comparison, plus the Coaches Poll. Before we get too carried away arguing about humans versus computers, we should probably find out whether the humans agree with each other. Or the computers, for that matter. The comparisons below use the preseason AP and Coaches polls and both analytics models' ratings from the morning of November 1, before the season began. Kansas and Iowa State get more respect from the computers The top of the board offers relatively little controversy. Both human polls put Florida first and Duke second. Both analytics models reverse that order. Illinois is third in both polls and fourth in both models. Everybody likes those three teams. After that, things get more interesting. The blue-blood Kansas Jayhawks represent one of the biggest disagreements entering this season, and the surprising part is who likes them more. It’s the computers. Kansas is No. 17 in the AP Poll and tied for 18th in the Coaches Poll. KenPom has the Jayhawks fifth and TeamRankings puts them sixth. I would have expected the voters to be higher on a historically great program like Kansas. Seeing both computers put the Jayhawks in the top six while neither human poll has them in the top 15 definitely caught me by surprise. Iowa State is another team where we see major disagreement. The Cyclones were a No. 2 seed in the 2026 NCAA Tournament but enter this season ranked 18th by the AP and tied for 14th with the coaches. KenPom has them sixth. TeamRankings puts Iowa State 11th, higher than either human poll but below KenPom. The Cyclones’ defense helps explain KenPom’s optimism: he projects it to be the second-best unit in the country. Alabama is another program getting more love from the models. The Crimson Tide are 20th in the AP Poll and tied for 18th in the Coaches Poll, compared with ninth in KenPom and 16th at TeamRankings. KenPom projects Alabama to have the nation’s fourth-best offense. Houston rounds out that group. The Cougars are third in KenPom and seventh at TeamRankings, ahead of their placements in the AP Poll (10th) and Coaches Poll (eighth). KenPom gives Houston the top defensive projection in the country. Tennessee and USC get more love from the human polls USC might be the best example of why this exercise is worth doing. Both groups of voters awarded the Trojans a preseason Top 25 ranking (21st by the AP and 22nd by the coaches), while neither model placed the Trojans inside the top 35. KenPom has them 37th, and TeamRankings puts them 40th. Tennessee presents an even more interesting argument near the top of the polls. The Volunteers are eighth in the AP and ninth in the Coaches Poll. The analytics are considerably less impressed: 22nd in KenPom and 18th at TeamRankings. If you followed last year's series, that might sound a little backward. Tennessee was a KenPom favorite last preseason, sitting ninth in the model compared with 18th in the AP Poll. This time, the voters are the optimistic ones. For what it’s worth, the Volunteers reached the Elite Eight as a No. 6 seed before losing to top-seeded Michigan. Arkansas belongs on the watch list, too. The Razorbacks are 12th in the AP Poll and 13th with the coaches, but KenPom places them 19th and TeamRankings has them 25th. The Razorbacks reached the Sweet 16 in 2026. JOHN CALIPARI JOKES THAT HE WAS 'ON CRACK' WHEN PUTTING TOGETHER ARKANSAS' WILDLY DIFFICULT SCHEDULE BYU lands 25th in both human polls, while both models leave the Cougars outside the Top 25: 34th in KenPom and 30th at TeamRankings. St. John’s offers another familiar disagreement: AP No. 13 and tied for 14th with the coaches, compared with 21st in KenPom and 17th at TeamRankings. Last preseason, the AP had the Red Storm fifth while KenPom ranked them 16th. The gap is smaller this time, but the voters are higher on St. John’s again. Nebraska gets more attention from the analytics this time Nebraska was one of the best stories in last year's series because neither side saw the Huskers coming. They began outside KenPom's top 50 without receiving a single preseason AP vote, then climbed into the top 15 of both rankings by our March update. This year's starting positions are very different. KenPom has Nebraska 15th and TeamRankings puts the Huskers 22nd. The human voters at least noticed Nebraska this year. The Cornhuskers are just outside both Top 25s, effectively 27th in the AP Poll and 26th in the Coaches Poll. Nebraska is coming off a 28-7 season that included the first Sweet 16 appearance in program history. Ohio State is another unranked team KenPom likes, placing the Buckeyes 18th. TeamRankings has them 31st, though, which brings us to the complication with treating "the analytics" as a single opinion. Vanderbilt and UConn divide the computers Vanderbilt should be familiar to anyone who read these columns last season. KenPom consistently liked the Commodores more than the AP voters did, and the same disagreement is back. Vanderbilt is 12th in KenPom, compared with 24th in the AP Poll and 21st with the coaches. After following these rankings last season, I think the humans put more weight on how teams finished the previous year. Vanderbilt didn’t make it out of the first weekend of the NCAA Tournament, and I suspect that’s part of why the voters aren’t as high on the Commodores as KenPom is. TeamRankings has Vanderbilt 24th, exactly where the AP puts the Commodores, so KenPom is sort of on an island here with its optimism for the Commodores in 2026-27. UConn gives us a different split. The Huskies are fourth in the AP Poll and fifth in the Coaches Poll. That's not surprising considering UConn is coming off a national championship game appearance and won back-to-back titles in 2023 and 2024. KenPom isn't as high on Dan Hurley's squad, though, and ranks them 11th. This seems like a slam-dunk case of the humans being on board with a perennial powerhouse while the analytics see a team set to take a step back. Except TeamRankings has UConn third, making the model more optimistic than either human poll. Louisville offers a smaller version of the same argument. Both human polls have the Cardinals 11th, between KenPom at 16th and TeamRankings at ninth. We'll also see whether one model outperforms the other and whether the coaches do a better job than the media. Want something included in the next "CBB With Danny Z"? articles.title: Lawyers rush to halt Indiana execution over state’s lethal drug supplier
articles.summary: Hours before Indiana was poised to carry out its first execution of the year, set for Thursday before sunrise, lawyers and supporters for the condemned man rallied to spare his life after new details emerged about the state’s secretive process of obtaining lethal injection drugs.
articles.body: Hours before Indiana was poised to carry out its first execution of the year, set for Thursday before sunrise, lawyers and supporters for the condemned man rallied to spare his life after new details emerged about the state’s secretive process of obtaining lethal injection drugs. Attorneys for Jeffrey Weisheit, 50, called on Indiana Gov. Mike Braun to halt his lethal injection execution and order an independent review of the state’s procedures over allegations that the state obtained its chemicals from a pharmacy currently on probation and facing suspension of its license. “Laid bare, the apparent conduct here is patently unworthy of the public’s confidence in the solemn exercise of state power in taking a human being’s life in the name of the people,” Joe Perkovich, an attorney for Weisheit, said in a statement Wednesday. Weisheit, who was convicted in the 2010 murders of two young children in a house fire, did not contest his guilt but sought clemency from Braun for his sentence to be commuted to life in prison without parole. His attorneys are citing Tennessee’s failed lethal injection execution of Christa Pike on Sept. 30 in his new application to the governor seeking a reprieve, saying Indiana’s protocol is “more susceptible to catastrophic failures such as the one that placed Ms. Pike in a coma,” and that the pharmacy listed on a state Department of Correction invoice has a history of “rampant mishandling of drugs.” An updated inventory log provided to NBC News shows that the Department of Correction added six vials of the lethal drug, pentobarbital, to the prison supply on Oct. 29. An invoice included in the reprieve application says that the state paid $275,000 for those vials — far higher than the typical $15,120 to $16,250 price for commercially made injectable pentobarbital. The invoice is heavily redacted and shows neither the date nor supplier for the transaction. Indiana law shields the identities of participants, pharmacies and suppliers involved in carrying out executions. However, a September 2025 invoice for the same dollar amount that corresponds with the last time the state added vials of pentobarbital to its supply accidentally revealed the possible supplier of the drug, according to exhibits included in Weisheit’s application for a reprieve. The exhibits were produced by the Department of Correction in response to a records request related to Weisheit’s execution date. An address retrievable from beneath a black redaction corresponds to the address for Pharmaneek, an Indianapolis-based pharmacy. Pharmaneek is scheduled to appear before the Indiana Board of Pharmacy on Monday — four days after Weisheit’s scheduled execution — over allegations that the pharmacy violated its probation after failed inspections by the Indiana Professional Licensing Agency and the Food and Drug Administration. The inspections found that Pharmaneek stored drugs in unlabeled bottles, found bottles of expired drugs “on random inspection of active pharmacy shelves” and failed to keep consistent temperature logs for pharmacy storage areas. In a settlement agreement with the state, Pharmaneek said some inspection problems were due to remodeling. According to an FDA inspection report from March 2026, the “facility is not maintained in a good state of repair, creating unsanitary conditions whereby drug products may be contaminated with filth.” The FDA report says its findings do not represent a final agency determination of compliance. Indiana licensing records for Pharmaneek that correspond with details listed on the Department of Correction invoice show that the pharmacy’s license and controlled substance registration are on probation. According to a legal filing dated Sept. 24, the Indiana Board of Pharmacy, which investigates complaints and can issue penalties, ordered Pharmaneek to appear before its members on Oct. 5 to “show cause” why its pharmacy license “should not be suspended on an emergency basis or subjected to the imposition of further sanctions.” A motion from Pharmaneek’s legal counsel included in the reprieve application shows that a lawyer for the pharmacy asked that the appearance be moved to Monday. Pharmaneek did not respond to NBC News’ multiple requests for comment this week by phone. The Indiana Department of Correction also did not respond to requests for comment or an interview. The governor’s office declined to comment Wednesday on the allegations that the Department of Correction obtained execution drugs from a pharmacy on probation. While Pharmaneek is currently barred from mixing custom drugs — a process known as compounding — Weisheit’s reprieve application alleges the pharmacy is acting as a middleman for the Department of Correction, supplying it with manufactured pentobarbital the department is not permitted to purchase straight from traditional drug manufacturers. In court filings prior to the execution of Roy Lee Ward in October 2025, the state said the pentobarbital it planned to use was produced by a pharmaceutical company instead of a compounding pharmacy, and distributed “without any post-manufacturing customizations.” Major drug companies have explicitly warned states not to use their drugs for executions and have sued states for the return of their chemicals. Sagent Pharmaceuticals, one of two pharmaceutical companies that manufacture pentobarbital in the United States, did not respond to emailed questions about whether it has a relationship with Pharmaneek; however, the company’s policies do not allow its distributors or wholesalers to sell its products to prisons for use in lethal injection. The other, the drugmaker Hikma, said the company does not have a purchase agreement with Pharmaneek. “We have strict prohibitions and controls intended to prevent the use of our medicines in capital punishment,” said Steven Weiss, a Hikma representative. A spokesperson for Indiana Attorney General Todd Rokita told NBC News the office is “confident in the ability to safely and lawfully carry out the scheduled execution.” They added that Weisheit’s lawyers “have publicly identified a pharmacy that they claim is connected to Indiana’s execution-drug supply, despite state law requiring supplier information to remain confidential.” Weisheit has been on death row for 13 years after a Vanderburgh County jury convicted him of murdering Alyssa Lynch, 8, and her brother, Caleb, 5, the children of his then-girlfriend, Lisa Lynch. She had been at work while Weisheit was watching the children in their Evansville home. Prosecutors said Weisheit bound and gagged Caleb, then placed railroad flares in his clothing and near his body before setting fire to the home and fleeing out of state. Alyssa’s body was found in a closet. The children had died of smoke inhalation. Weisheit appealed his conviction, including on the grounds of ineffective counsel, but was denied relief. Last month, Weisheit appeared at a clemency hearing in front of the state parole board, during which his mental illness and other health struggles were discussed. He was unable to offer a reason for why he killed the Lynch children. “There is no excuse or explanation for what I did,” Weisheit said. Lisa Lynch asked the board to uphold his death sentence and keep the focus on her children. “Every birthday, every holiday, every landmark moment is marked by their agonizing absence,” she said. “Time passes, but the weight of losing them never fades.” The children’s father, Steven Lynch, told the board that he supported clemency and forgave Weisheit for his actions. The board ultimately recommended Braun deny clemency, which he agreed Monday not to grant. Lisa Lynch could not be reached for comment ahead of Weisheit’s scheduled execution. Steven Lynch told NBC News that he still hopes Weisheit can be shown mercy and said he was thinking of the convicted killer’s own family as they brace for a finite loss like the one he experienced when his own children were murdered. “No parent should have to outlive their child,” Steven Lynch said, adding that “mercy is extended to even the least of us.” Weisheit’s planned execution is one of three set for Thursday, with the others to be carried out by lethal injection in Alabama and Florida.
